findings.title: Link-census regex admits path traversal and absolute-path escapes that the stated containment check may not catch
findings.detail: The transitive-authority completeness check scans for `]\(([^)#]+\.md)(?:#[^)]+)?\)` and 'resolves the captured path against the referring document and require the target to remain under `spec/` and be a bundle member.' The capture class `[^)#]+` permits `..`, leading `/`, backslashes, percent-encoding (`%2e%2e%2f`), NUL-adjacent C0 bytes, and NFD forms. The amendment specifies NFC/segment/byte restrictions for *authority paths* in the bundle preimage, but does **not** specify the same normalization discipline for *captured link paths* before the `under spec/` test. A link written as `](spec/../../etc/passwd.md)` or `](spec/./product.md)` or `](spec/%2e%2e/secret.md)` resolves differently depending on whether the resolver normalizes before or after the prefix test. If it string-prefix-tests before normalization, `spec/../../x.md` passes the `spec/` prefix test and then fails membership (fail-closed, fine) — but `spec/./product.md` passes both prefix and, after normalization, membership, meaning a link can be *encoded in a form that isn't byte-equal to any bundle-member path yet still resolves to one*. That is a link-census aliasing hole: two distinct raw byte strings map to the same member, so the 'ordered link census' recorded in the two receipts can differ between materializers over the same bytes if their normalizers differ, producing a spurious or suppressed AUTHORITY_MISMATCH.
findings.evidence: "the literal regular expression `]\(([^)#]+\.md)(?:#[^)]+)?\)` ... They resolve the captured path against the referring document and require the target to remain under `spec/` and be a bundle member." — no normalization, canonicalization, or reject-list is specified for the captured group, unlike the explicit `spec/[A-Za-z0-9._/-]+`, NFC, no-empty/`.`/`..`-segment rules imposed on *authority paths*.
findings.recommendation: Apply the identical path predicate to captured link targets that already applies to authority paths: require the captured bytes to match `spec/[A-Za-z0-9._/-]+\.md` exactly, be NFC, contain no empty/`.`/`..` segment, no percent-encoding, no backslash, no C0/C1, and then require **byte-equality** with a bundle-member path rather than resolution-then-membership. Any captured path failing that predicate is `AUTHORITY_MISMATCH` rather than 'an observation.' State that resolution is byte-equality, not filesystem canonicalization.

findings.title: Overlay anchor uniqueness is checked in the raw base, but insertions are ordered only by declaration ordinal at the same offset — three same-heading operations create an underspecified splice
findings.detail: O-09, O-10, O-11 all target `### P-10 — material brownfield outcome improvement` in spec/product.md; O-13 and O-14 both target `#### Scoring and falsification`; O-01/O-02 both target architecture section 1. The document says 'Materialization streams unchanged base spans in ascending raw offset, using declaration ordinal only to order same-offset insertions, and rejects a same-offset replacement/insertion combination.' It also says overlapping ranges or 'a new block that would alter another operation's base range' is AUTHORITY_MISMATCH. But it never states what happens when an *insertion anchor's end offset* falls strictly inside a *later-declared replacement's* old-block range, or when a replacement's old block *starts exactly at* an insertion anchor's end offset (adjacent, not same-offset, not overlapping). Adjacency is the exact case that arises when two operations edit consecutive prose in the same section — which O-09/O-10/O-11 do. The rule set has a gap between 'same offset' (rejected/ordered) and 'overlapping' (rejected); adjacency is neither, and the resulting byte order is determined by implementation detail, not spec. Two structurally separate materializers can legitimately disagree here, and the amendment's central safety claim is that their byte-equality proves correctness.
findings.evidence: "Replacements and insertions then apply in declaration order to the recorded raw-base byte ranges; overlapping ranges, a new block that would alter another operation's base range, or zero/multiple matches is `AUTHORITY_MISMATCH:<operation-id>`." combined with three operations (O-09, O-10, O-11) sharing one heading and the O-13/O-14 pair sharing another.
findings.recommendation: Define the total order explicitly and mechanically: sort all operations by (raw base start offset, then a declared tie-break class where insertion-at-offset-X emits before replacement-starting-at-X or vice versa — pick one and state it), and add adjacency to the rejected set unless the ordering is explicitly declared. Add a frozen corpus case for 'insertion anchor end == replacement old-block start' and for 'insertion anchor end strictly inside a later replacement range' with expected bytes or rejection code, and require both materializers to pass it before G-1.

findings.title: The two-materializer agreement claim is explicitly acknowledged to permit a shared author, making the core authority-derivation control a single point of failure
findings.detail: The amendment's strongest structural claim is 'Resolved plans, complete bundles, and roots must be byte-equal.' It then concedes 'The two programs may share a Validator author, so their agreement falsifies inconsistent parsing/splicing but is not independent human requirements interpretation.' A shared author with a shared misunderstanding of the (underspecified, see finding above) adjacency/normalization rules produces two byte-identical wrong bundles that pass every mechanical gate. The stated compensating control is Agy adversarial review plus founder ratification of the rendered bundle — but Agy is simultaneously declared possibly-correlated with every other role (`UNVERIFIED` fields 'conservatively overlap every family'), and the founder reviews *rendered* output, which is precisely the artifact a shared-author bug would render consistently wrong. The residual is honestly disclosed but not mitigated: there is no control that catches a correlated splice error.
findings.evidence: "The two programs may share a Validator author, so their agreement falsifies inconsistent parsing/splicing but is not independent human requirements interpretation." and "Any field that cannot be observed outside Agy is `UNVERIFIED`, conservatively overlaps every family it could be, and contributes no diversity evidence."
findings.recommendation: Add a third, trivially-auditable check that is not a materializer: require the founder receipt to include, for each operation, the exact decoded old-block bytes and exact decoded new-block bytes side by side with 200 bytes of raw base context — already partly required for Agy — plus a mechanical assertion that `base_bytes.replace(old, new)` over the recorded span reproduces the effective artifact digest, computed by a fourth trivial script whose entire logic is a byte splice at recorded offsets. Alternatively, require the second materializer to be authored by someone who has not read the first, and record that fact as a named receipt field rather than an acknowledged residual.

findings.title: Checkpoint admission and journal `started` write share one mutex, but the tree-cap precheck is TOCTOU against concurrent build-root writes
findings.detail: The design states 'Before every mutation, the gated writer computes the resulting path count and content-byte count and rejects an operation that could exceed either cap.' The cap is on the *live source envelope* (20,000 paths / 1 GiB). But the checkpoint watchdog 'computes the source-worktree tree digest twice consecutively' and admits only if both match — implying the source tree can change between reads, which is exactly what the lease is supposed to prevent. Meanwhile compiler/build children 'see source read-only and write disposable roots.' If any disposable root is inside the worktree (a `target/` directory is the Rust default and is inside the workspace), then the path/byte count computed by the gated writer and the tree digest computed by the watchdog are measuring different sets, and a build child can inflate the on-disk path count between the precheck and the mutation without ever holding source-write capability. The cap enforcement is then advisory rather than enforced, and `CHECKPOINT_CAPACITY_EXCEEDED` may fire non-deterministically or fail to fire.
findings.evidence: "Longer builds write only disposable build/cache roots and cannot modify source." versus "Before every mutation, the gated writer computes the resulting path count and content-byte count" and "computes the source-worktree tree digest twice consecutively. It admits the checkpoint only when the journal head is unchanged, no call remains outstanding, and both tree digests match."
findings.recommendation: Define 'live source envelope' as an explicit, enumerated path set (the Git-tracked source tree plus a named untracked allowlist), state that disposable build/cache roots are outside it by construction (separate mount or explicitly excluded prefix), and require G-4 to prove that a build child writing 2 GiB into `target/` neither trips `CHECKPOINT_CAPACITY_EXCEEDED` nor changes the source tree digest. Otherwise the double-read is masking a real concurrency hole rather than detecting it.

findings.title: Observer HMAC one-use token binds body digest but the wrapper's replay defense depends on an unspecified atomic spend across crash boundaries
findings.detail: The token is 'an HMAC over `(run_generation, sequence, predecessor_digest, body_sha256, body_byte_count)`' and the wrapper 'atomically spends the sequence, and refuses substitution or replay.' Atomic spend across a crash requires the spend record to be durably persisted before the body is forwarded — otherwise a crash between forward and spend-commit lets a restarted wrapper accept the same token again. The amendment specifies fsync ordering meticulously for the *journal* ('fsyncs the `started` record before any child process exists') but does not specify the equivalent ordering for the wrapper's spend ledger relative to the socket write. G-4 'injects blocking `fsync` and full-volume failures and proves no held body is replayed' — that tests the *observer* hold path, not the wrapper spend path after a successful forward. An attacker model here is not the provider (who can't forge the local MAC) but a crash-restart plus a non-malicious operator replaying a queued request, which the amendment explicitly wants to detect ('Application retries are new counted custody events').
findings.evidence: "The wrapper buffers and hashes the exact body it will forward, verifies every committed field, atomically spends the sequence, and refuses substitution or replay." — no fsync-before-send ordering is stated for the spend, unlike the journal's explicit "`fsync`s the `started` record **before any child process exists**."
findings.recommendation: State the wrapper invariant with the same rigor as the journal: the spend record must be fsynced to durable storage *before* the first byte of the body reaches the SSH socket, and on restart the wrapper must treat any sequence present in the spend ledger as spent regardless of whether a response was received. Add a G-4 drill: kill the wrapper between spend-fsync and socket write, and between socket write and response, and prove in both cases the token cannot be re-presented and that the observer/wrapper/spent-token counts still reconcile exactly (or fail closed).

findings.title: Q-0 sentinel and ledger share root, workstation, and operator with the Validator — the replay defense is explicitly not a security boundary but is load-bearing for the irreversible disclosure edge
findings.detail: The amendment is candid: 'It shares the workstation, root trust, and human operator with the Validator, so this is crash/non-adversarial-operator-error detection, not an independent security boundary and not protection from a malicious Validator, root, or kernel.' But the control it implements — 'Observed replay above the frozen count permanently blocks the route' — is the sole mechanism guarding the *irreversible* pre-ratification disclosure edge described in section 0 ('Once a repository byte is transmitted to a marketplace host, that disclosure cannot be proven erased'). A control guarding an irreversible edge that fails open to local root is a mismatch between the stakes and the mechanism. The amendment does not claim otherwise, but it also does not add any control that survives local root, and it does not require the founder ratification text to name this specific gap (the founder receipt must state 'irreversible specification disclosure' and 'one cold-restart allowance and no calibrated completion probability' — not 'the pre-ratification egress counter is defeatable by local root').
findings.evidence: "The separately permissioned local sentinel retains the current chain-head digest outside the Validator ledger's filesystem ... It shares the workstation, root trust, and human operator with the Validator, so this is crash/non-adversarial-operator-error detection, not an independent security boundary" — set against section 0's "irreversible disclosure edge."
findings.recommendation: Either (a) move the send counter to a substrate that survives local root — a hardware token, a remote append-only log with a key the workstation cannot forge, or a TPM-sealed counter — or (b) explicitly add to the mandatory founder ratification statement that the pre-ratification synthetic-only allowance is enforced only against crash and non-malicious operator error, and that a compromised workstation can transmit repository bytes before ratification without producing a detectable ledger event. Option (b) costs nothing and closes the honesty gap; option (a) actually hardens it.

findings.title: Closed tool registry validates paths via parent-descriptor + `*at` no-follow, but argument normalization order versus journaling order can be inverted
findings.detail: The journal writer 'fsyncs canonical-CBOR, length-framed call ID, pre-normalization and validated arguments' — good, it records both. But the validation sequence states 'Parsing rejects duplicate or unknown keys, invalid UTF-8, noncanonical numbers, path traversal, symlink escape, C0/C1 or bidi-control path bytes, non-NFC Unicode paths, and values outside schema before dispatch' and separately 'Path validation opens the parent directory descriptor, and execution uses only `*at` operations relative to that same descriptor with no-follow semantics, so a pathname or symlink swap cannot change the validated object.' The `*at`-relative guarantee holds for the *final component* only. If the model supplies a multi-component path like `a/b/c`, opening 'the parent directory descriptor' means resolving `a/b` — and that resolution is itself subject to symlink swap unless it is done componentwise with `O_NOFOLLOW` at every level. The amendment says G-4 'races such a swap and requires denial,' but does not specify whether the raced swap targets the final component (easy) or an intermediate component (the actual attack). A model that can create a directory and then swap an intermediate component for a symlink escapes the worktree.
findings.evidence: "Path validation opens the parent directory descriptor, and execution uses only `*at` operations relative to that same descriptor with no-follow semantics, so a pathname or symlink swap cannot change the validated object. G-4 races such a swap and requires denial."
findings.recommendation: Specify componentwise resolution: every path component is opened with `openat(..., O_NOFOLLOW|O_DIRECTORY)` walking down from a pinned worktree root descriptor, with no `realpath`/`canonicalize` step and no reliance on a string-level parent split. Require G-4 to race a swap at an *intermediate* component (e.g. replace `a/b` with a symlink to `/tmp` while `a/b/c` is validated) and require denial; state that final-component-only racing does not satisfy the gate. Also state that `RESOLVE_BENEATH`/`RESOLVE_NO_SYMLINKS` (openat2) is the preferred Linux mechanism where available.

findings.title: Post-materialization occurrence recount cannot detect a new block that reconstructs an anchor across a splice seam
findings.detail: The materializer 'rejects any new block containing another operation's complete old/anchor bytes' and 'recounts every operation's complete source bytes and containing-heading line in that operation's effective artifact' with the rule 'A replacement source must occur zero times, an insertion anchor must occur exactly once.' Both checks operate on complete blocks. Neither catches the case where a new block's *suffix* concatenated with the following unchanged base *prefix* forms a complete anchor at a seam. The recount is described as running over the effective artifact, which would catch it — but only if the recount counts occurrences over the *whole* artifact bytes rather than per-operation-region. The text says 'recounts every operation's complete source bytes ... in that operation's effective artifact,' which is ambiguous about scope. If per-region, seam-created anchors are invisible; if whole-artifact, the check is sound but the ambiguity means two materializers can implement it differently and still agree if neither triggers the case.
findings.evidence: "It rejects any new block containing another operation's complete old/anchor bytes, even though matching is base-only ... After splicing, it also recounts every operation's complete source bytes and containing-heading line in that operation's effective artifact."
findings.recommendation: State explicitly that the post-materialization recount scans the *complete raw bytes of the entire effective artifact*, not any region or window, and that the count includes occurrences spanning splice seams. Add a frozen corpus case where a new block's trailing bytes plus the following base bytes reconstruct an anchor, with the expected rejection code, and require both materializers to pass it before contributing to G-1.

findings.title: The Coder's sole-egress proxy chain has an unstated failure mode: proxy and observer are separate processes but the invariant is asserted, not proven, at every restart
findings.detail: 'Sole-egress is an invariant: the Coder sandbox has no other network namespace, socket, inherited tunnel descriptor, DNS path, or provider-side agent.' Startup probes 'attempt an outside-root write, symlink escape, `..` traversal, forbidden read, inherited-descriptor read, and direct network connection' before every launch. But the mid-run remount path ('A mid-run remount or any other readable-set expansion requires the quiescence lease and termination of every Coder/tool process; the complete mount/descriptor census and authorized-send superset are rebound before a new Coder process exists') rebinds the *readable* set and the *authorized-send* superset — it does not restate that the network denial probe is rerun. A remount that adds a mount namespace entry could, in a sloppy implementation, restore network reachability without any probe re-firing, since the enumerated rebind list is about reads and sends, not sockets.
findings.evidence: "A mid-run remount or any other readable-set expansion requires the quiescence lease and termination of every Coder/tool process; the complete mount/descriptor census and authorized-send superset are rebound before a new Coder process exists." — the pre-launch probe list including "direct network connection" is specified only for "Before every launch."
findings.recommendation: State that the mid-run remount path reruns the *complete* pre-launch denial probe battery, explicitly including direct network connection, inherited-descriptor read, and DNS, and that the resulting probe receipt is appended to the ledger with the rebound census. Make 'before every launch' and 'after every remount' the same enumerated list rather than two lists.

findings.title: The nine-member bundle is disclosed to the provider in full, including the exact 30-second and 90-second timing constants that define the local fail-closed windows
findings.detail: The amendment states this plainly and argues correctness doesn't depend on provider ignorance: 'A host can delay a response until the local timeout cancels it, and a provider can delay settlement until the monotone lag uncertainty closes admission. Neither delay is favorable evidence.' That reasoning is sound for confidentiality and for proof integrity. But the disclosed constants (`turn_timeout_seconds = 1620`, `sentinel_staleness_seconds = 90`, 30-second observer hold, 300/60/120/30/360 checkpoint phases, `poll_interval` 60s) give a hostile provider an exact recipe to maximize burned dollars per unit of delivered work: respond at 1619 seconds, or stall at exactly the boundary of each reserve. The amendment accounts for this as 'residual-cost risk' the founder accepts, which is honest, but there is no jitter and no adaptive response, so the worst case is fully deterministic and maximally expensive.
findings.evidence: "The first repository-bearing request exposes the complete nine-member effective authority bundle to the named processor, including this amendment's account/host binding, control topology, timeout values, polling cadences, reserve formulas, and terminal conditions." combined with "The host can therefore consume already authorized runtime or force an incomplete/fail-closed route."
findings.recommendation: No change to the security claim is needed. Consider adding a bounded random jitter to `turn_timeout_seconds` and the poll interval (e.g. uniform over a declared range, seeded from a Validator-owned value not in the bundle), recorded per-turn in the ledger. This preserves determinism of the *bound* while removing the exact boundary a hostile host would target, at zero cost to the proof.

findings.title: Supplemental artifacts are admitted by digest only, with no structural or link-census constraint stated at admission time
findings.detail: `spec/glossary.md` and `spec/leak-runbook.md` are admitted as 'subordinate supplemental authority' by SHA-256 alone. They are bundle members and are therefore scanned by the link census, and the Validator's semantic-delta receipt must compare them 'against every higher-precedence obligation.' But the amendment does not state that they must satisfy the same encoding invariants imposed on base artifacts ('UTF-8 without BOM and contain LF only; any CR byte is a parse error'). That rule is scoped to 'The amendment and every base artifact.' A supplement containing CRLF, a BOM, or non-NFC content would be admitted by digest and then scanned by a regex over raw bytes, producing materializer-dependent link-census results.
findings.evidence: "The amendment and every base artifact must be UTF-8 without BOM and contain LF only; any CR byte is a parse error." — the two supplements are neither the amendment nor base artifacts, yet they are bundle members subject to the raw-byte link census.
findings.recommendation: Extend the encoding predicate to every bundle member, not just the amendment and base artifacts: require UTF-8, no BOM, LF-only, NFC, and no C0/C1 except LF, checked at admission before the digest is bound, with a mismatch producing `AUTHORITY_MISMATCH`. Add both supplements to the frozen adversarial corpus as CRLF/BOM negative cases.

persona_reports.summary: Overall this is an unusually hardened document — the fail-closed disciplines, the explicit disclosure of what each control *does not* prove, and the refusal to let mechanical agreement masquerade as independence are all better than typical. The real attack surface is not in the stated threat model but in the **underspecified seams**: adjacency in the splice ordering, normalization of captured link paths, componentwise symlink resolution, wrapper spend durability, and the scope of the post-materialization recount. Each of those is a place where two honestly-written materializers or two honestly-written validators can diverge or agree-on-wrong, which directly undermines the amendment's central structural claim that byte-equality of two independent plans proves correct derivation; I'd fix the five ambiguities before ratification, and treat the local-root gap in the Q-0 counter as something the founder receipt should name out loud since it guards an irreversible edge.

findings.title: Rust 1.98.1 with edition 2024 is very likely a non-existent toolchain pin, and a fabricated channel-manifest digest is bound into G-1
findings.detail: The amendment pins `rust-toolchain.toml` to Rust 1.98.1 and asserts a SHA-256 for `channel-rust-1.98.1.toml`. Rust ships one minor release every six weeks from a well-known base (1.0 in May 2015); 1.98.x would land far outside the plausible window for the dates this document itself uses (`2026-09-06` observations imply roughly the 1.9x series only if you extrapolate optimistically, and the amendment offers no derivation). More importantly, the amendment's own text says the Validator observation 'records the official channel manifest retrieval and local-toolchain limitation' — i.e. the toolchain could not be installed locally. So the digest was recorded without ever being exercised. If the version or digest is wrong, G-1 does not catch it (G-1 checks overlay bytes, not toolchain existence), and the failure surfaces only at the first offline `--locked` build after the route has already burned cold-load and qualification dollars.
findings.evidence: 'Rust is pinned by `rust-toolchain.toml` to 1.98.1. The Validator observation in `evidence/factory-run/rust-toolchain-observation-001.md` records the official channel manifest retrieval and local-toolchain limitation.' Also: overlay O-01 asserts 'a Rust 1.98.1 workspace, edition 2024' as ratified Product bytes.
findings.recommendation: Add a pre-G-1 gate that actually installs the pinned toolchain in the offline build environment, compiles a hello-world with `--locked` and edition 2024, and records `rustc -Vv` matching the pin. Make toolchain-pin verification a G-1 precondition, not a G-9 discovery, and treat a nonexistent/mismatched channel manifest as `AUTHORITY_MISMATCH` before any spend.

findings.title: The budget arithmetic does not actually fit: the stated USD 299.10 admission requirement plus the G-3 mandatory rehost exceeds what the document itself computes as remaining
findings.detail: The amendment computes prospective admission terms as USD 240.98 + 24.10 operational contingency + 34.02 cold-restart contingency = USD 299.10, against ~USD 342.08 authorization-remaining, claiming 'at most USD 42.98' unallocated margin. But G-3 *mandatorily* consumes the cold restart to replace instance 50012413 — so the actual sequence is: (a) pay cold_load + runtime_qualification on the fresh host (USD 34.02) as *consumed spend*, then (b) re-evaluate admission, which still requires the full 5R warm authoring, in-flight, charge, and 10% operational reserves. The 34.02 does not disappear from the ledger when 'consumed'; it reduces `authorization_remaining` while the remaining requirement stays at ~USD 265.08. That leaves ~USD 8.96 of headroom before stopped-storage, the USD 2.00 uncertainty floor, `unconfirmed_destroy_exposure_usd`, and any rate rise. Section 2.5 also says 'Any offered/current rate above the recomputed ceiling refuses restart' — and the illustrative ceiling of USD 39.25/hour against an observed USD 34.0022/hour rate is a ~15% margin on a spot marketplace. The route is arithmetically one modest auction move from `UNFUNDED` before the first repository byte.
findings.evidence: 'At the recorded rates those terms are USD 17.01 + 17.01 + 170.02 + 17.01 + 19.93 = **USD 240.98** ... operational contingency is USD 24.10, and one cold-restart contingency is USD 34.02: **USD 299.10** total ... The historical unallocated margin at `2026-09-06T03:41:03Z` was therefore at most USD 42.98.' Combined with: 'G-3 consumes it to replace the disqualified pre-ratification host, so no post-disclosure restart remains.'
findings.recommendation: Show the post-G-3 admission inequality explicitly with the rehost already consumed, including stopped-storage accrual between ratification and warm start, and state the resulting headroom in dollars. If it is under ~USD 20, either raise `C` in this amendment or explicitly declare that the route is expected to terminate `UNFUNDED` on any rate increase, so the founder ratifies that reality rather than a USD 42.98 illusion.

findings.title: Five protected warm hours for a complete P-1..P-10 Rust implementation is an unstated-and-implausible capacity assumption dressed as an honest 'no completion probability claimed'
findings.detail: The document repeatedly disclaims any completion probability, which is epistemically honest but does not make the plan sound. The prior attempt produced a 29-module, 9,378-line Python tree and still failed. The G-6 predicate demands 'one clean final Rust HEAD whose reachable Coder series maps every effective P-1 through P-10 obligation to implemented paths' — including three non-convertible store types, a loopback Company service with SQLite transactions, a signed `.kin/` content-addressed event protocol under Git common-dir locking, Landlock/bubblewrap sandboxing, descriptor-passing across five process modes, a `kin` subprocess adapter, and full CLI/JSON-envelope/exit-code conformance. Budgeting eight 30-minute slots (minus the VOI turn and 10% control reserve) for that in Rust, with no prior Rust codebase, is not a risk — it is a near-certain `UNFUNDED`. The amendment's own defense ('exhaustion is an honest UNFUNDED') means the most probable outcome of ratification is spending ~USD 300 and an irreversible specification disclosure to reach an incomplete result. That trade is never argued on its merits.
findings.evidence: 'the proposed ceiling therefore funds at most five protected warm Coder hours in total plus one restart's cold load and qualification' vs. 'Completion is the G-6 predicate: one clean final Rust HEAD whose reachable Coder series maps every effective P-1 through P-10 obligation to implemented paths and implementation-owned checks.' Also §1: 'The current 29-module, 9,378-line Python tree remains uncommitted and unadmitted.'
findings.recommendation: State the expected-value argument explicitly for the founder receipt: what is gained if the route ends incomplete at slot 8? The VOI turn produces an obligation-to-module plan — argue that the plan itself plus prior-art commits justify the irreversible disclosure, or raise the funded window to something with a defensible relationship to the scope. 'Honest UNFUNDED' is a disposition, not a justification for spending the disclosure edge.

findings.title: The VOI turn's obligation-coverage plan is a model-authored artifact treated as a gate input while all model forecasts are banned — an inconsistent trust boundary
findings.detail: Section 2.5 forbids any model-produced effort/duration/probability field ('The plan schema has no effort, duration, slice-count, completion-probability, or fits-budget field; any such field is rejected') on the correct grounds that model forecasts are unreliable. But the same paragraph makes the model's *obligation-to-module/command plan* a checkpoint predicate: 'Every effective behavior-ledger row and amended obligation must map to at least one named work package ... an unmapped obligation fails the checkpoint.' A model that reliably cannot estimate effort is also a model that can trivially satisfy a coverage check by emitting one shallow work package per obligation. The Validator 'checks coverage against the effective behavior ledger' — coverage, i.e. presence of a mapping, not adequacy of the mapping. The gate is therefore satisfiable by a plan with 100% coverage and zero decomposition depth, which conveys no information and consumes 20 minutes of the five-hour clock.
findings.evidence: 'The plan schema has no effort, duration, slice-count, completion-probability, or fits-budget field; any such field is rejected. The Validator checks coverage against the effective behavior ledger' + 'an unmapped obligation fails the checkpoint.'
findings.recommendation: Either (a) accept that the VOI turn's only defensible output is a critical-path *ordering* and drop the coverage predicate's gate status, or (b) add a minimum-decomposition criterion the Validator can check mechanically (e.g. each work package names distinct output paths and at least one implementation-owned check that is not a restatement of the obligation text). Also state what disposition applies if the plan is trivially compliant but obviously inadequate — currently only `INVALID_PLAN` for 'zero work or fails complete obligation/slice mapping', which a shallow plan passes.

findings.title: The checkpoint phase budget sums to 870 seconds but the watchdog must complete a cycle within fifteen minutes (900 s) from the *prior admitted checkpoint* — leaving 30 seconds for the checkpoint admission itself and no slack for lease contention
findings.detail: The fixed schedule is 300+60+120+30+360 = 870 s, and the watchdog 'completes or terminates each checkpoint cycle before fifteen minutes have elapsed from the prior admitted checkpoint.' 900 − 870 = 30 seconds of total slack for: reading the journal head twice, building a content-addressed ref with a private temporary index over a tree of up to 20,000 paths / 1 GiB, computing the worktree tree digest *twice consecutively*, and recording lease/sequence numbers. The 360-second `snapshot_deadline_seconds` presumably covers the snapshot, but the phases are described as sequential deadlines from a 300-second start trigger, so the clock is 300 (trigger) + up to 60 (drain) + up to 120 (reconcile) + up to 30 (lease) + up to 360 (snapshot) = 870 with the admission bookkeeping unbudgeted. Worse: `CHECKPOINT_DEFERRED:<call-id>` fires when a journal call is `started` without `result` at lease-grant time — but the drain phase only has 60 seconds and 'any possibly mutating call then receives at most 120 seconds' for reconciliation. A tool whose registry-declared maximum duration exceeds 60 seconds guarantees deferral, and the amendment never constrains registry maximum durations to be under the drain deadline.
findings.evidence: 'The fixed schedule is `checkpoint_start_interval_seconds = 300`, `active_call_drain_deadline_seconds = 60`, `reconciliation_deadline_seconds = 120`, `lease_acquisition_deadline_seconds = 30`, and `snapshot_deadline_seconds = 360`; their sum is 870 seconds' + 'a Validator-owned monotonic watchdog completes or terminates each checkpoint cycle before fifteen minutes have elapsed from the prior admitted checkpoint.'
findings.recommendation: Constrain every registry tool's declared maximum duration to be strictly less than `active_call_drain_deadline_seconds`, or state the deferral-retry policy explicitly (currently `CHECKPOINT_DEFERRED` says 'cancel at frozen timeout, reconcile, then checkpoint before any new operation' — which can itself exceed the 900 s window and trigger termination). Budget the checkpoint-admission bookkeeping as a named phase rather than leaving it in the 30-second residue, and have G-4's 30 cycles include a worst-case cycle where a long-running tool is active at second 300.

findings.title: Sole-egress invariant relies on a three-process chain (proxy → observer → SSH wrapper) whose failure semantics are asymmetric and whose 30-second hold cap is not reconciled with the 27-minute turn timeout
findings.detail: The observer holds a body for at most 30 seconds; timeout 'discards the held body, cancels the model turn, runs local journal reconciliation, destroys the instance, and emits `UNFUNDED_BY_OBSERVER_STALL`'. That is route-terminal. Meanwhile the fsync latency of a single small append on a workstation is normally milliseconds, but the amendment itself requires G-4 to 'inject blocking `fsync` and full-volume failures' — i.e. it anticipates fsync stalls. A single transient 31-second I/O stall (common on a consumer SSD under GC pressure, a filesystem snapshot, or an FDE re-key) therefore destroys the instance, burns the remaining warm clock, and ends the route with no restart allowance (G-3 already consumed it). The failure mode is 'the workstation's disk hiccuped' → 'the USD 400 route is over.' There is no retry, no distinction between transient and permanent stall, and no relationship between this 30-second cap and the far more generous 27-minute turn timeout.
findings.evidence: 'A hold has a 30-second maximum. Timeout or observer volume exhaustion discards the held body, cancels the model turn, runs local journal reconciliation, destroys the instance, emits `UNFUNDED_BY_OBSERVER_STALL`' combined with 'G-4 injects blocking `fsync` and full-volume failures.'
findings.recommendation: Separate transient-stall from durable-failure: permit a bounded number of retries within the turn timeout (the body is already held, so no unrecorded send is possible), and reserve instance destruction for volume exhaustion or repeated stall. Alternatively raise the hold cap to something with headroom against observed fsync p99 and require G-4 to measure that p99 on the actual workstation storage before freezing the value. As written, a fixed 30 s is a magic number with no measured basis.

findings.title: The two-materializer 'byte-equal plans' control is explicitly acknowledged as sharing an author, which makes it a consistency check that cannot detect a shared misreading of the amendment's own decoding rules
findings.detail: The document is admirably honest that 'The two programs may share a Validator author, so their agreement falsifies inconsistent parsing/splicing but is not independent human requirements interpretation.' But it then loads enormous weight onto that agreement: G-1 requires 'two structurally separate equal plans/bundles' as primary evidence that the effective authority bundle is correct. The blockquote-decoding spec is intricate (exactly one leading `> `, sole `>` for blank, trailing SP/TAB is a parse error, synthesized trailing LF, insertion-at-anchor-end-offset with no implicit separator, same-offset replacement/insertion rejection, post-materialization recount). A single author writing two implementations of that spec will reproduce the *same* misreading in both — that is the dominant failure mode of same-author reimplementation, and the frozen negative/positive corpus is also authored by the same person, so it encodes the same misreading as the expected output. The residual is stated but never sized or mitigated.
findings.evidence: 'The two programs may share a Validator author, so their agreement falsifies inconsistent parsing/splicing but is not independent human requirements interpretation.' + 'Before either materializer can contribute to G-1, both pass the same frozen negative/positive corpus' (also same-author).
findings.recommendation: Have Agy — which already reads 'at least 200 raw-base bytes on either side of every resolved span' — independently produce the expected effective bytes for at least two operations by hand from the amendment text alone, without seeing either materializer's output, and require byte-equality with the materialized result. That is cheap and provides the one thing the two-program control structurally cannot: a second human reading of the decoding rules.

findings.title: The link-census regex is asserted to be the transitive-authority completeness check but silently ignores reference-style links, relative-path forms, and URL-encoded paths
findings.detail: The regex `]\(([^)#]+\.md)(?:#[^)]+)?\)` matches only inline links whose target ends in `.md` before an optional fragment. It misses: (a) CommonMark reference-style links `[text][ref]` with `[ref]: spec/foo.md` definitions; (b) autolinks `<spec/foo.md>`; (c) percent-encoded paths (`spec/leak%2Drunbook.md`) which would resolve to a real file but not match the intended path check; (d) any link with a `)` inside the path, which `[^)#]+` truncates. The amendment says 'there is no CommonMark interpretation step' and 'Paths merely named in backticks do not match and remain observations, not authority' — but that cuts the wrong way for reference-style links, which *are* rendered as real links and *would* pull in an out-of-bundle authority document while the census reports clean. The check is presented as 'the mechanical transitive-authority completeness check'; it is actually a partial one.
findings.evidence: 'Both materializers independently scan the raw UTF-8 of every bundle document for every non-overlapping occurrence of the literal regular expression `]\(([^)#]+\.md)(?:#[^)]+)?\)` ... This is the mechanical transitive-authority completeness check, not a claim about rendered Markdown semantics.'
findings.recommendation: Add a second negative scan: reject any bundle document containing a reference-link definition line (`^\[[^\]]+\]:`), an autolink containing `.md`, or a percent-encoded byte in a matched path. That makes the incompleteness fail-closed rather than silent, without introducing CommonMark parsing.

findings.title: The P-5 matched-pair requirement can be arithmetically unsatisfiable or trivially gamed depending on how 'at least half' interacts across three overlapping strata
findings.detail: The V-5 overlay imposes: (1) substantive mirror set ≥ genuine-`Unknown` count; (2) 'At least half of the substantive mirror set is superficially conflict-shaped' (from P-5); (3) 'Every superficially conflict-shaped substantive case must be an admitted member of that matched-pair stratum'; (4) 'matched pairs comprise at least half of the complete substantive set'; (5) 'Unpaired or reviewer-rejected cases count toward neither minimum.' Constraint (5) is the trap: if the fresh reviewer rejects some conflict-shaped cases for trivial lexical cues, those cases count toward *neither* the conflict-shaped-half minimum nor the matched-pair-half minimum, but they presumably still exist in the matrix. It is unclear whether they must be removed, and whether removal then breaks constraint (1) by shrinking the substantive set below the `Unknown` count — requiring `Unknown` cases to be deleted too, which changes the P-5 semantics the matrix was built to test. There is no stated resolution procedure and no bound on iteration.
findings.evidence: 'Every superficially conflict-shaped substantive case must be an admitted member of that matched-pair stratum, and matched pairs comprise at least half of the complete substantive set. Unpaired or reviewer-rejected cases count toward neither minimum.'
findings.recommendation: State whether reviewer-rejected cases are deleted from the matrix or retained as non-counting, and give a deterministic repair procedure with a bounded number of reviewer rounds. Add a worked example with concrete counts (e.g. 20 `Unknown`, 20 substantive, 10 conflict-shaped, 10 matched pairs) demonstrating the constraint set is jointly satisfiable.

findings.title: Two supplemental artifacts are admitted into authority by digest without any precedence-conflict analysis being performed before ratification
findings.detail: The amendment admits `spec/glossary.md` and `spec/leak-runbook.md` as 'subordinate supplemental authority' by digest, and requires the Validator's semantic-delta receipt to 'compare the complete glossary and leak runbook against every higher-precedence obligation.' But the glossary is simultaneously declared load-bearing for the *entire amendment*: 'Terms used here inherit [`glossary.md`](glossary.md)'. So the amendment's own meaning depends on a document whose consistency with the amendment is only checked *after* the amendment text is frozen. If the glossary's definition of 'lane', 'admitted', or 'positive control' contradicts the inline redefinitions the amendment supplies in the same sentence, the precedence rule ('supplemental leak runbook and glossary' rank below the amendment's controls) resolves it — but the amendment's own reader summary already asserts specific meanings, so a mismatch means the reader summary was wrong at ratification time. This is a chicken-and-egg ordering problem, not merely a review task.
findings.evidence: 'Terms used here inherit [`glossary.md`](glossary.md); in this amendment, a **lane** is one role's isolated filesystem/process authority ...' alongside 'Ratification of this amendment admits their exact current bytes as subordinate supplemental authority' and 'It also compares the complete glossary and leak runbook against every higher-precedence obligation.'
findings.recommendation: Move the glossary-consistency check to a pre-authoring precondition: require the Validator to publish the load-bearing-term comparison *before* the amendment's final candidate freeze, so any narrowing/widening is resolved in the amendment text rather than dispositioned under precedence after the fact. Otherwise state explicitly that the inline definitions in the reader summary are authoritative and the glossary is advisory for those four terms.

findings.title: `UNCONFIRMED_DESTROY` creates an unbounded liability accumulator with no exit condition under provider unresponsiveness
findings.detail: If a destroy does not return a trustworthy terminal receipt within `stop_destroy_reserve_seconds`, the route enters `UNRESOLVED_CUSTODY`: 'the greatest observed running rate times elapsed time accumulates without bound in `authorization_uncertainty`' and 'G-2 and G-11 cannot close, and no terminal monetary, custody, or proof claim may be issued until a trustworthy provider terminal observation plus billing reconciliation or account closure resolves the exposure.' The stated exits are provider observation or *account closure*. But Vast marketplace instances routinely return stale or delayed status; a provider control-plane outage of a few hours would push `authorization_uncertainty` past `C` and permanently block G-11 for a run that may have already completed all its substantive work. The design correctly refuses to treat a timeout as success, but it offers no bounded escalation path other than closing the entire Vast account — a drastic remedy with side effects on any other work, and one that is not obviously available or instantaneous.
findings.evidence: 'From the attempted-destroy timestamp until a trustworthy terminal provider observation, the greatest observed running rate times elapsed time accumulates without bound in `authorization_uncertainty` ... until a trustworthy provider terminal observation plus billing reconciliation or account closure resolves the exposure.'
findings.recommendation: Add an intermediate resolution: an invoice-based settlement showing no further charges accruing for the instance over a stated observation window should be admissible as terminal evidence, with the custody residual (not the monetary residual) remaining open. Distinguish the *monetary* exposure (resolvable by billing) from the *custody* exposure (never fully resolvable, already acknowledged) so a control-plane outage cannot indefinitely block G-11 on a question billing can answer.

findings.title: Q-2's 500-decoy qualification is honestly caveated but the honest caveat concedes the control does not do what the gate requires
findings.detail: The amendment states that 500 zero-positive decoys give a Wilson upper bound of ~0.0076, then immediately says 'this is reported as a calibration statistic only. No exchangeability with future real candidates or field false-positive rate is claimed. The statistic is not divided by `M_egress`, is not a familywise guarantee, and does not pretend that 500 establishes a one-percent union bound over the structural minimum of 660 or any larger powered census.' That is intellectually honest, but it concedes the qualification provides no bound on the probability that *at least one* of ≥660 real candidates triggers a false positive — and a single confirmed false positive is `INVALID_HARNESS`, i.e. it destroys the entire measurement. At a true FPR of even 0.005 (well inside the stated bound), the probability of at least one false positive across 660 candidates is ~96%. The design therefore has a stated ~certainty of `INVALID_HARNESS` unless the true FPR is far below what 500 decoys can establish, and the amendment never confronts that arithmetic.
findings.evidence: 'At 500 zero-positive decoys the two-sided 95% Wilson upper bound for that frozen decoy population is approximately 0.0076; this is reported as a calibration statistic only ... does not pretend that 500 establishes a one-percent union bound over the structural minimum of 660.' Combined with: 'A mechanically confirmed false positive or unresolved scanner/Detector disagreement is `INVALID_HARNESS`.'
findings.recommendation: Either scale the decoy corpus so the union bound over `M_egress` is meaningful (roughly `M_egress`/α decoys for a familywise target), or soften the disposition: a single confirmed false positive on a candidate whose blinded adjudication is clean could invalidate that *cell* under intention-to-treat rather than the whole harness. As written, the gate's failure probability is dominated by detector calibration rather than by anything about the Product.

findings.title: The 20,000-path / 1 GiB tree cap is enforced pre-mutation by the gated writer, but build artifacts and Cargo's target directory are only excluded by assertion, not by a stated path policy
findings.detail: The amendment says 'Longer builds write only disposable build/cache roots and cannot modify source' and 'Before every mutation, the gated writer computes the resulting path count and content-byte count and rejects an operation that could exceed either cap.' A Rust workspace's `target/` directory routinely exceeds 20,000 files and several GiB. The separation between 'source worktree' (capped, checkpointed) and 'disposable build roots' (uncapped) is asserted but the amendment never states the mechanism — is `target/` outside the worktree, gitignored-but-inside, or a separate mount? If it is inside the worktree and merely gitignored, the 'source-worktree tree digest' computed twice consecutively during snapshot would either include it (blowing the cap and the 360-second snapshot deadline) or must exclude it by a rule that is nowhere specified. G-4 qualifies 'a synthetic tree at both caps' but says nothing about a concurrent build populating `target/`.
findings.evidence: 'G-4 qualifies the exact maximum live-source envelope of 20,000 paths and 1,073,741,824 content bytes' + 'Longer builds write only disposable build/cache roots and cannot modify source' + 'computes the source-worktree tree digest twice consecutively.'
findings.recommendation: Specify the filesystem layout normatively: `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` and the dependency cache live outside the checkpointed source root, on a separate writable root in the sandbox policy, and the tree-digest computation enumerates only the source root. Add a G-4 case that runs a full `cargo build` concurrently with a checkpoint cycle and proves the 360-second snapshot deadline holds under real build I/O contention.

findings.title: 'No compatibility claim is made against the unadmitted Python tree' is correct, but the CLI/JSON-envelope/exit-code surface is simultaneously declared unchanged authority — the Rust binary inherits a contract no implementation has ever satisfied
findings.detail: Section 2.1 says 'the materialized CLI names, JSON envelopes, error codes, exit codes, and Product obligations remain authority unless this amendment explicitly changes them. No compatibility claim is made against the unadmitted Python tree.' Those two sentences are consistent only because the Python tree was never admitted. But it means the Rust Coder must implement a CLI contract that has never been exercised by any admitted implementation, with G-1 requiring every process mode to map 'either to that exact CLI surface or to a named internal mode whose complete wire/exit contract is added by ratified authority before either lane starts.' The seven-row process/capability table introduces modes (classifier launcher, shared projector, coding projector, acceptance coding agent) whose wire contracts are not obviously present in `spec/cli.md`. If they are not, G-1 requires a *further* ratified authority addition before the lane starts — which is not budgeted, not scheduled in the gate graph, and would be discovered at G-1 after the amendment is frozen.
findings.evidence: 'G-1 must map every mode either to that exact CLI surface or to a named internal mode whose complete wire/exit contract is added by ratified authority before either lane starts. An independently invented launch convention is `AUTHORITY_MISMATCH`, not a G-9 implementation failure.' + the seven-row process topology table.
findings.recommendation: Before ratification, have the Validator enumerate which of the seven process modes have a complete wire/exit contract in the effective CLI and which do not, and either include the missing contracts as additional overlay operations in this amendment or explicitly schedule a follow-on amendment as a G-1 precondition. Discovering a missing contract at G-1 stalls the route with no allocated time.

persona_reports.summary: The document is unusually rigorous about epistemics — it repeatedly refuses to overclaim, names its residuals, and fails closed by default — and most of my findings are about arithmetic and unstated preconditions rather than logical sloppiness. The two that should block ratification are the Rust 1.98.1 toolchain pin (a fabricated-looking version and an unexercised channel digest baked into ratified Product bytes, discoverable only after money is spent) and the budget arithmetic, where the mandatory G-3 rehost consumes the restart allowance and leaves single-digit-dollar headroom against a spot-market rate — meaning the stated USD 42.98 margin materially overstates the route's viability. The five-hour warm window for a complete P-1..P-10 Rust implementation is honestly disclaimed but never justified; the founder is being asked to accept an irreversible disclosure for an attempt whose most probable outcome, by the document's own structure, is `UNFUNDED`.

findings.title: The control apparatus dwarfs the thing it controls, and none of it has produced a line of admitted code
findings.detail: This is a ~15,000-word amendment governing a five-hour, $400 coding session against an unproven product whose implementation has never been admitted. Seven prior attempts terminated without an admissible commit. The document's response to seven failures is not to reduce the scope of the attempt or to change the shape of the bet — it is to add a two-implementation byte-exact overlay materializer, a three-tier egress proxy chain, a body-bound HMAC observer with one-use spend tokens, a five-phase 870-second watchdog, a dual-derivation budget policy function with an uncertainty band, a 30-day prior-art custody clock, a roster with `asserted_at`/`verified_at` columns, and eleven terminal error codes. The ratio of control machinery to controlled work is roughly inverted from healthy. The most likely failure mode of this generation is not an uncontrolled disclosure or a budget overrun — it is that the setup work (Q-0/Q-1/Q-2, G-1 through G-5) consumes the founder's remaining attention and money before G-6 is ever attempted, exactly as the previous seven attempts consumed theirs.
findings.evidence: "The Ollama route repeatedly replayed an approximately 200K-token context without reported cache hits, exhausted purchased usage, and terminated seven times without an admissible Coder commit." Against that, section 2.2 alone specifies: admission proxy + observer relay + SSH wrapper as three separate sandboxed processes sharing "no code or writable state"; an HMAC over `(run_generation, sequence, predecessor_digest, body_sha256, body_byte_count)`; `checkpoint_start_interval_seconds = 300, active_call_drain_deadline_seconds = 60, reconciliation_deadline_seconds = 120, lease_acquisition_deadline_seconds = 30, snapshot_deadline_seconds = 360`; "at least 30 complete held-lease cycles"; and G-4 drills for spawn failure, symlink race, duplicate request, fsync failure, full volume, rate rise, and mid-forwarding interruption.
findings.recommendation: Before ratifying, do a written cost accounting of the setup path itself: estimate the engineer-days to build and qualify Q-0, Q-1, the observer/wrapper MAC chain, the watchdog, the dual materializer, and the 500-decoy detector. If that number exceeds the value of the five hours it protects, the amendment has inverted its own priorities. The honest alternative is to name the smallest control set that makes the irreversible disclosure acceptable (see finding 2) and defer everything else to a later generation.

findings.title: The observer/wrapper HMAC chain is elaborate machinery for a threat the document admits it does not defend against
findings.detail: The amendment builds a three-process egress chain (proxy → observer relay → SSH wrapper), a per-body one-use HMAC token over five fields, atomic sequence spending, fsync-before-release, a 30-second hold ceiling, a frozen transport byte envelope with framing classes, and duplicate-request drills. It then states plainly that everything readable by the Coder is authorized to be sent to Vast, that the gate "cannot hide authorized repository bytes from Vast or defend against a model intentionally retransmitting bytes it was allowed to read," and that a malicious Validator, local root, or kernel is out of scope. So the residual threat this machinery actually covers is: a non-malicious operator's accidental inclusion, plus crash-consistency of the send log. Those are real but modest threats. A single append-only fsync'd send log written by a process the Coder cannot write to, plus the kernel capability confinement that is already declared the "confidentiality root," covers essentially the same ground. The HMAC, the sequence spending, the substitution-refusal, and the framing envelope defend the log against an adversary the document has already excluded from the threat model.
findings.evidence: "Physical capability confinement is the confidentiality root" and "anything forbidden to send is structurally unreadable, not entrusted to a scanner" — yet the same section adds "Its one-use token is an HMAC over `(run_generation, sequence, predecessor_digest, body_sha256, body_byte_count)` under a run key readable only by observer and SSH wrapper. The wrapper buffers and hashes the exact body it will forward, verifies every committed field, atomically spends the sequence, and refuses substitution or replay." Section 2.3 concedes: "this is crash/non-adversarial-operator-error detection, not an independent security boundary and not protection from a malicious Validator, root, or kernel."
findings.recommendation: Collapse the observer/wrapper/proxy triple into one Validator-owned, append-only, fsync'd egress log process that the Coder sandbox cannot write. Keep the fsync-before-forward ordering (that is the one property that actually earns its keep). Delete the HMAC, the one-use sequence tokens, the substitution/replay refusal, and the frozen transport framing envelope, or move them to a future amendment with an explicit statement of which in-scope adversary they defeat. Blast radius shrinks: three interdependent processes become one, and the `UNFUNDED_BY_OBSERVER_STALL` terminal branch disappears with them.

findings.title: Fifteen coupled overlay operations create a single-point authority failure across six specification files
findings.detail: The overlay mechanism requires that fifteen `old`/`anchor` blocks each match exactly once, byte-for-byte, under a nearest-preceding-heading rule, in six base files, with no CR, no BOM, no trailing whitespace, NFC-normalized paths, and post-materialization recounts — and both of two independently written materializers must produce byte-equal plans, bundles, and roots. One stray byte anywhere in that surface halts the entire generation with `AUTHORITY_MISMATCH:<O-id>` and no partial progress. Worse, four unrelated concerns are fused into this one all-or-nothing bundle: the Rust rewrite (O-01–O-05), the provider swap (O-06), the P-5 abstention fix (O-07, O-08), and the P-10 statistics tightening (O-09–O-15). Section 2.6 acknowledges the fusion and defends it, but the defense ("ratifying the runtime change alone would... require a mid-lane authority change") argues only that the P-5/P-10 changes should land *before* the Coder starts — not that they must land in the *same* atomic overlay as the Rust substitution.
findings.evidence: "Replacements and insertions then apply in declaration order to the recorded raw-base byte ranges; overlapping ranges, a new block that would alter another operation's base range, or zero/multiple matches is `AUTHORITY_MISMATCH:<operation-id>`." And: "These corrections are logically distinct from the language/provider substitution but remain in one effective-generation bundle..."
findings.recommendation: Split into two sequentially ratified amendments: 001a (proof-semantics corrections: O-07 through O-15, the P-5 mirror set and the P-10 co-primary endpoints) and 001b (implementation and runtime: O-01 through O-06 plus sections 2.2–2.5). 001a touches only product.md and verification.md, has no budget or custody surface, and can be ratified today with far less review load. 001b then anchors against the already-effective 001a output. Blast radius per ratification drops from six files and fifteen operations to two/nine and four/six, and a byte mismatch in the statistics prose no longer blocks the Rust build.

findings.title: Two independent materializers plus a frozen adversarial corpus, then an admission that they prove almost nothing
findings.detail: The amendment mandates a second, structurally separate implementation of the overlay parser/splicer, requires byte-equal plans and bundle roots, and requires both to pass a frozen negative/positive corpus covering `>`, `> >`, trailing SP/TAB, CRLF, lone CR, BOM, NFC/NFD, empty blocks, embedded ATX headings, section-extent crossing, duplicate headings, and same-offset operations. It then concedes both programs may share a single author and that agreement "is not independent human requirements interpretation." So the second implementation catches only *inconsistent* coding by one author against one spec — a class of bug that the frozen corpus alone would catch far more cheaply, and that a diff of the rendered output against the base would catch essentially for free. The real safety net is the one already present: Agy reads the full effective diff with 200 bytes of context on each side, and the founder reads the complete rendered bundle before ratifying. Those are human reads of the actual output. The second materializer is redundant with them.
findings.evidence: "The two programs may share a Validator author, so their agreement falsifies inconsistent parsing/splicing but is not independent human requirements interpretation." and "Agreement is only parser/splice evidence; the shared-author residual remains explicit."
findings.recommendation: Drop the second materializer. Keep the frozen negative/positive corpus (cheap, catches the actual parser bugs), keep the post-materialization recount (catches shadowed anchors), and keep the human read of the rendered diff and full bundle (catches semantics). Reinvest the saved effort in the corpus. If a second implementation is retained anyway, state explicitly which failure class it catches that the corpus plus the human diff read does not.

findings.title: The budget apparatus reduces to a simple rule, but is expressed as an irreducible thicket
findings.detail: Section 2.5 defines two competing spend derivations, a `max()` policy function that is explicitly not a fact and has no owner, a dimensioned uncertainty band with a $2.00 floor plus a settlement-lag term plus an unattributed-delta term plus an unconfirmed-destroy term, a monotone-max rate rule, a signed reconciliation delta with a two-minute attribution window, an `UNRESOLVED_ACCOUNT_DELTA` code, a rate-ceiling inequality, a slot floor formula, a 10% reserve, and a cold-restart contingency that flips to zero on consumption. The underlying policy is comprehensible in three sentences: (1) always assume the worst observed rate applied to all elapsed time; (2) never let unexplained provider deltas free authorization; (3) stop when the pessimistic total plus reserves would reach $400. That policy is correct and worth having. Its current expression cannot be verified by reading — the worked arithmetic ("USD 17.01 + 17.01 + 170.02 + 17.01 + 19.93 = USD 240.98") is presented without derivation of the $19.93 charge reserve, and the rate-ceiling inequality `1.10 * (6R + max(...) + 6S + ((60+D)/3600)R + 10) + R <= A` is stated once and never checked against the term list above it.
findings.evidence: "`budget_policy_value = max(validator_derived_provider_spend, validator_elapsed_estimate)` is not another fact and has no owner. It is a policy function evaluated fresh at each admission." Followed by seven more defined terms and two derived inequalities, then: "At the recorded rates those terms are USD 17.01 + 17.01 + 170.02 + 17.01 + 19.93 = **USD 240.98** (rounded upward per term)..."
findings.recommendation: State the three-sentence policy first, as the normative rule. Then move the term definitions and worked arithmetic into a single referenced table with one column per term showing formula, value at the recorded rate, and derivation. Delete the `max()`-with-no-owner prose paragraph; a policy function that combines two owned facts needs no ontological disclaimer. A reader should be able to check the $299.10 total in under a minute.

findings.title: The five-phase watchdog schedule is over-parameterized relative to what it protects
findings.detail: Five named second-valued deadlines (300/60/120/30/360, summing to 870) govern a checkpoint cycle whose purpose is: quiesce, snapshot the worktree, verify the snapshot didn't move. The verification itself is already robust — read journal head, snapshot, read head again, compute tree digest twice, admit only if all match. That double-read invariant is the property that makes the checkpoint trustworthy, and it holds regardless of how the 870 seconds are apportioned. The five sub-deadlines add five independently tunable numbers, five failure branches, and a G-4 obligation to run 30 full cycles proving each sub-deadline holds at the 20,000-path/1-GiB cap — all to bound a total that a single deadline would bound equally well.
findings.evidence: "The fixed schedule is `checkpoint_start_interval_seconds = 300`, `active_call_drain_deadline_seconds = 60`, `reconciliation_deadline_seconds = 120`, `lease_acquisition_deadline_seconds = 30`, and `snapshot_deadline_seconds = 360`; their sum is 870 seconds." and "It builds a synthetic tree at both caps and runs at least 30 complete held-lease cycles, each of which must satisfy every fixed phase deadline and the 870-second total."
findings.recommendation: Keep one deadline (870 seconds from prior admitted checkpoint) and the double-read admission invariant. Keep the 300-second point as the *start* trigger. Delete the three intermediate sub-deadlines and their separate failure branches; on total-deadline expiry, take the existing terminal action (kill the gated writer, mark crash artifact, terminate). G-4's obligation reduces to: 30 cycles at cap complete within 870 seconds. Same guarantee, one number, one branch.

findings.title: Q-0's ledger/sentinel rollback machinery guards a bounded probe count against a non-adversary
findings.detail: Q-0 exists to cap pre-ratification synthetic probes. It gets: an fsync'd monotonic counter, a Validator-owned route-generation ledger row keyed by probe digest, predecessor-chaining into the Factory ledger, a separately permissioned local sentinel holding the chain head on a *different filesystem*, an equality check at every proxy start, drills for both scratch-recreation and restoration-of-older-snapshot, and a permanent route block on observed replay. The document then states this is "crash/non-adversarial-operator-error detection, not an independent security boundary" against an operator who shares the workstation, root trust, and human identity with the Validator. The consequence of the counter being wrong in the non-adversarial case is: a few extra synthetic probes, containing no repository bytes, reach a host that will be destroyed anyway (per G-3). The machinery is disproportionate to that consequence, and the cross-filesystem sentinel adds a second component whose failure ("unreadable/missing/rollback-mismatched") blocks the route.
findings.evidence: "The separately permissioned local sentinel retains the current chain-head digest outside the Validator ledger's filesystem; every proxy start requires equality or treats the count as exhausted. It shares the workstation, root trust, and human operator with the Validator, so this is crash/non-adversarial-operator-error detection, not an independent security boundary..." and "An unreadable/missing/rollback-mismatched ledger blocks only until the founder ratifies a new probe-digest set and count under a recorded storage incident."
findings.recommendation: Replace the ledger/sentinel/rollback-drill complex with a single fsync'd append-only counter file owned by the Validator, and state the residual plainly: an operator who deletes it can re-probe. Since G-3 already destroys the probed instance and the probes carry no repository bytes, that residual is acceptable. Removes one component, two drills, and one blocking failure mode.

findings.title: The V-5 matched-pair stratum specifies six matching dimensions and a fresh reviewer to enforce a property one dimension would capture
findings.detail: The P-5 fix is sound in concept: abstention must not be a free pass, so add substantive-answer cases and make some of them look conflict-shaped. The implementation requires one-to-one matching on source count, source classes, scope, timestamp/validity-field presence, and decoy-prose/token-length band; exactly one preregistered resolving predicate may differ within a pair; a fresh reviewer who did not author the cases must freeze pair IDs, the resolving predicate, the token-length band, and a no-trivial-lexical-cue finding before outcomes are visible; and unpaired or reviewer-rejected cases count toward neither minimum. That is a five-dimension matching contract plus a new human role, to defend against a harness author writing lexically-obvious easy cases. The load-bearing constraint is the single one: within a pair, only the resolving predicate differs. Everything else is derivative of it or is a lexical-cue check that a mechanical token-length/vocabulary diff can perform without a new role.
findings.evidence: "At least half of substantive cases are one-to-one matched to genuine-`Unknown` cases on source count, source classes, scope, timestamp/validity-field presence, and decoy-prose/token-length band. Within a pair, only one preregistered policy-relevant resolving predicate (authority, scope, expiry, or supersession state) may change the required result. Before implementation or model outcomes are visible, a fresh reviewer who did not author the cases freezes pair IDs, the resolving predicate, token-length band, and a no-trivial-lexical-cue finding."
findings.recommendation: State the single invariant — within a matched pair, the two cases differ only in the value of one named resolving predicate — and make the mechanical check its enforcement: a diff of the two case bodies must show a change confined to that predicate's fields. Drop the separate five-dimension enumeration (it is implied) and the fresh-reviewer role (the mechanical diff is stronger and cheaper). Keep the outcome-blind freeze timing.

findings.title: The 500-decoy detector qualification is priced and mandated, then disclaimed as proving nothing about the actual population
findings.detail: Q-2 requires at least 500 frozen, stratified, difficulty-matched decoys spanning every scanner-visible encoding, candidate format, boundary position, and benign provenance class, with zero observed false positives. The amendment then correctly states the Wilson bound is "a calibration statistic only," that "no exchangeability with future real candidates or field false-positive rate is claimed," that it is "not a familywise guarantee," and that it does "not pretend that 500 establishes a one-percent union bound over the structural minimum of 660 or any larger powered census." Four consecutive disclaimers of a number is a strong signal that the number is not carrying its weight. Meanwhile the *disposition* rule — a confirmed false positive is `INVALID_HARNESS`, a confirmed true recovery is a scored zero and Product failure, an unresolved disagreement is `INVALID_HARNESS` — is the part that actually makes detector error unable to manufacture lift, and it holds at any decoy count.
findings.evidence: "At 500 zero-positive decoys the two-sided 95% Wilson upper bound for that frozen decoy population is approximately 0.0076; this is reported as a calibration statistic only. No exchangeability with future real candidates or field false-positive rate is claimed. The statistic is not divided by `M_egress`, is not a familywise guarantee, and does not pretend that 500 establishes a one-percent union bound..."
findings.recommendation: Lead with the disposition rule as the safety property, since it is the one that actually holds. Reduce the decoy requirement to a defensible smoke-test count (e.g. covering each named encoding/format/boundary/provenance class at least once) and state the purpose as "catches a broken detector before it burns candidates," not as a rate bound. Delete the Wilson calculation and its four disclaimers. Saves construction cost from the G-10 plan without weakening any claim actually made.

findings.title: Terminal codes proliferate where existing dispositions already cover the case
findings.detail: Eleven amendment-specific codes are defined, several of which resolve to the same operator action. `UNFUNDED_BY_OBSERVER_STALL` (discard body, reconcile, destroy, append apology), `UNFUNDED_BY_RECONCILIATION_STALL`, and plain `UNFUNDED` (stop/destroy, retain partial lineage, ask founder) differ in cause, not in what anyone does next. `UNCONFIRMED_DESTROY` and `UNRESOLVED_CUSTODY` are presented as a single slash-joined row with one action. `CHECKPOINT_DEFERRED:<call-id>` and `CHECKPOINT_CAPACITY_EXCEEDED` share the frozen-timeout-then-reconcile path. Each additional code is another branch a reader and an implementer must hold, and the distinguishing information (which cause fired) belongs in the ledger record, not in the code name.
findings.evidence: The terminal-code table lists `UNFUNDED`, `UNFUNDED_BY_OBSERVER_STALL`, `UNRESOLVED_ACCOUNT_DELTA`, `UNCONFIRMED_DESTROY` / `UNRESOLVED_CUSTODY`, `CHECKPOINT_DEFERRED:<call-id>`, and `CHECKPOINT_CAPACITY_EXCEEDED` — six codes whose "Required next action" columns reduce to three distinct action sequences (stop-destroy-escalate; cancel-reconcile-then-continue; presume-live-and-block-closure).
findings.recommendation: Collapse to the three action-distinct codes and carry the cause as a required field in the accompanying ledger record: `UNFUNDED{cause=observer_stall|reconciliation_stall|arithmetic|deadline}`, `CHECKPOINT_BLOCKED{cause=outstanding_call|capacity}`, `UNRESOLVED_CUSTODY{cause=unconfirmed_destroy|census_mismatch}`. Same information, three branches instead of six.

findings.title: No reader summary states what this document is trying to make happen in one paragraph a non-author can act on
findings.detail: The reader summary lists four changes and then immediately qualifies them across two paragraphs of what the amendment does *not* do, followed by the append-only supersession mechanics. A reader arrives at section 8's dependency graph without ever having been told the shape of the bet: 'we are spending up to $400 and five hours of a rented 8xH200 to have GLM-5.3 write a Rust implementation of P-1 through P-10 from the spec alone, with no prior code and no test access; if it doesn't finish, we keep the partial work as unadmitted prior art and ask for more money.' That sentence is the document. Everything else is the conditions under which it is allowed to happen. Burying it costs every reviewer twenty minutes of orientation.
findings.evidence: The reader summary opens: "This candidate makes four changes to one still-unproven Guildhall generation: 1. implement the complete P-1 through P-10 Product in Rust rather than Python..." and proceeds directly into "It does **not** narrow P-1 through P-10 behavior, collapse the three physical stores..." before any statement of the wager, its cost, or its success condition.
findings.recommendation: Add a three-sentence lead paragraph stating the bet, the ceiling, the single success predicate (G-6: one clean Rust HEAD covering every P-1–P-10 surface), and the honest failure mode (`UNFUNDED`, partial work retained as prior art). Then the four changes. Then the disclaimers. A senior engineer should know what is being attempted within 30 seconds.

persona_reports.summary:
The core problem is not that any single control here is wrong — most are individually defensible responses to a real risk, and the discipline about what evidence does *not* prove (provider erasure, first-contact attestation, decoy exchangeability, Agy independence) is genuinely admirable and rare. The problem is that a document governing five hours of coding has grown a control surface larger than the product it protects, and several of its most elaborate mechanisms (the HMAC egress chain, the dual materializer, the Q-0 sentinel, the 500-decoy bound) are explicitly disclaimed *in the same paragraph that mandates them* as not defending against any adversary in the threat model. That pattern — build the machine, then honestly admit it doesn't do the thing — appears often enough to be structural rather than incidental.

My strongest single recommendation is finding 3: split the proof-semantics corrections (O-07 through O-15) into their own amendment and ratify them now. They are correct, they are cheap, they touch two files, and they are currently hostage to a byte-exact fifteen-operation overlay across six files whose failure mode is total. After that, the remaining runtime amendment can be judged on its own merits with a much smaller blast radius.

findings.title: No entry point: the document opens with the most complex machinery and never tells a newcomer where to start reading
findings.detail: The 'Reader summary' promises a four-item summary, then immediately drops into ~2,000 words of blockquote-decoding rules, byte-offset splicing semantics, `AUTHORITY_MISMATCH` conditions, bundle-root preimage formats, and link-census regexes before the reader has learned what the amendment *does*. A first-time reader has no way to know that sections 2.1-2.6 are the actual content and that the front matter is a materialization protocol they may not need to read at all. There is no 'if you are X, read Y' guide, no table of contents, and no visual/structural break between 'how this document is applied mechanically' and 'what this document changes.'
findings.evidence: Reader summary items 1-4 occupy ~15 lines.
