They are immediately followed by 'This is an append-only amendment candidate to manifest ac8a13...' and then approximately eight dense paragraphs on blockquote decoding, anchor uniqueness, byte ranges, and materializer equality — all before section 0. Section numbering starts at 0 (Stakes), so the entire front matter is unnumbered and unaddressable.
findings.recommendation: Split the front matter into a numbered section (e.g. '§-1 Materialization protocol') and move it after the substantive sections, or into a sibling document. Add a short 'How to read this' block at the top: founder reads §0, §2, §5-7; Validator reads the materialization protocol and §8; Coder reads only the materialized bundle, never this file.

findings.title: The operational checklist is 'section 8' but section 8 is a gate table, not a checklist — the actual procedure is scattered across the prose
findings.detail: The Reader summary states 'The operational checklist is section 8.' A reader turning to section 8 finds a dependency graph, an evidence table, and an error-code table — but not an ordered list of actions. The actual steps a Validator must perform (dry-run overlay, emit per-operation receipts, run the frozen adversarial corpus, materialize nine artifacts, compute bundle root, obtain Agy disposition, obtain founder receipt, create run binding) are described only in narrative prose in the unnumbered front matter, in a different order than they must be executed, and interleaved with justification. Someone following 'section 8' will miss steps.
findings.evidence: 'The operational checklist is section 8.' vs. section 8's actual content: a `text` dependency graph, a nine-row gate table with 'Required evidence' cells that are 60-100 word run-on sentences, and two more tables. The G-1 'Required evidence' cell alone contains at least nine distinct required artifacts separated by semicolons.
findings.recommendation: Add a genuine ordered procedure — numbered steps with the artifact each produces and the failure code for each — either as §8.0 or as a separate `spec/amendment-001-runbook.md`. Break the G-1 evidence cell into a sub-list.

findings.title: Error codes are defined in three different places with no single authoritative index
findings.detail: A user hitting an error needs one lookup table. Instead, `AUTHORITY_MISMATCH` semantics are defined in the front matter (at least six distinct trigger conditions across five paragraphs), `UNSUPPORTED_UNPROVEN_PLATFORM` in §2.1, `UNFUNDED_BY_OBSERVER_STALL` and `UNFUNDED_BY_RECONCILIATION_STALL` in §2.1/§2.5, `UNRESOLVED_ACCOUNT_DELTA` in §2.5, `CHECKPOINT_DEFERRED` in §2.1, and then a partial recap table in §8. `UNFUNDED_BY_RECONCILIATION_STALL` appears in §2.5 prose but is absent from the §8 code table entirely. `INVALID_PLAN` appears in the §8 table but its triggering condition is never stated in the body prose — §2.5 describes rejecting plan schema fields and requiring obligation mapping, but never names the code.
findings.evidence: §8 code table lists 13 codes. `UNFUNDED_BY_RECONCILIATION_STALL` (defined in §2.5: 'emits UNFUNDED_BY_RECONCILIATION_STALL plus a Validator-owned apology') is not among them. Conversely `INVALID_PLAN` in the §8 table ('VOI plan reports zero work or fails complete obligation/slice mapping') has no corresponding emission point in §2.5's VOI description.
findings.recommendation: Make the §8 code table exhaustive and normative. For each code, cite the section that emits it. Add `UNFUNDED_BY_RECONCILIATION_STALL`. Add an explicit emission sentence for `INVALID_PLAN` in §2.5. State whether the codes list is closed.

findings.title: `AUTHORITY_MISMATCH` is overloaded across ~9 distinct failure classes with no way to distinguish them
findings.detail: The same bare code `AUTHORITY_MISMATCH` (sometimes with an operation ID suffix, sometimes without) is emitted for: supplemental-artifact digest mismatch, a downstream role reading a superseded base file, rerunning the overlay in an author lane, an amendment control contradicting a higher-precedence artifact, an independently invented CLI launch convention, and — with an ID suffix — zero/multiple matches, overlapping ranges, path/heading disagreement, and post-materialization count violations. A user who receives `AUTHORITY_MISMATCH` with no suffix has no idea which of five unrelated conditions fired, and the doc gives no diagnostic guidance beyond 'no dispatch; repair as a new candidate.'
findings.evidence: Bare `AUTHORITY_MISMATCH` appears for: 'a digest mismatch is AUTHORITY_MISMATCH' (supplemental table); 'reading a superseded base file or rerunning the overlay inside an author lane is AUTHORITY_MISMATCH'; 'any contradiction is AUTHORITY_MISMATCH' (precedence); 'An independently invented launch convention is AUTHORITY_MISMATCH, not a G-9 implementation failure.' Meanwhile the §8 table only documents the suffixed form `AUTHORITY_MISMATCH:<O-id>`.
findings.recommendation: Introduce distinct sub-codes (e.g. `AUTHORITY_MISMATCH:SUPPLEMENT_DIGEST`, `:LANE_READ`, `:PRECEDENCE`, `:CLI_CONVENTION`) or at minimum require every emission site to carry a machine-readable reason field, and document them in §8.

findings.title: Named entities Agy, Codex, Claude, Kindex/kin, and Simulacrum are used as load-bearing terms with no in-document definition
findings.detail: The document says terms 'inherit glossary.md' and then defines only four terms inline (lane, run generation, admitted, positive control). But `Agy`, `Codex`, `Claude`, `Simulacrum`, `Advocate`, `kin`/Kindex, and `Vast` are used throughout as if the reader knows what they are, and it is not stated whether they are products, roles, vendors, or people. The reader cannot tell whether 'Agy' is a person, a model, or a script — which matters enormously because §2.3 spends a paragraph on whether Agy can be labeled independent. Similarly 'Codex root remains Validator' reads as a category error to a newcomer: is Codex a program whose root user is the Validator, or is 'Codex root' the name of a role?
findings.evidence: 'Agy remains the resident non-authoring Orchestrator with only `block` and `no-op` effects. Codex root remains Validator. Claude remains the implementation-blind Tester.' No antecedent defines any of these three. Later: 'the Validator hashes the invoked executable' for Agy dispositions — implying Agy is an executable — but 'Agy's own prose is not identity evidence' implies it produces text like a model.
findings.recommendation: Add a short 'Actors' table near the top: name, kind (human / model / vendor / executable / role), and what authority it holds. Even if glossary.md defines them, a self-contained actor table costs ten lines and removes the single largest comprehension barrier.

findings.title: The Q-0/Q-1/Q-2 control table introduces three named controls whose scope is only clear after reading three separate prose passages
findings.detail: Q-0, Q-1, and Q-2 are referenced in §0 ('Q-0 existed'), §2.1, §2.3, §2.4, §3, §4, and §8 before the reader reaches the table in §2.3 that actually defines them. §0 says 'the synthetic probes already sent to instance 50012413 before Q-0 existed' — the reader has no idea what Q-0 is at that point. This is a forward-reference chain three sections deep.
findings.evidence: §0: 'This control is prospective and cannot retroactively qualify the synthetic probes already sent to instance `50012413` before Q-0 existed.' The Q-0 definition table appears in §2.3, roughly 6,000 words later.
findings.recommendation: Move the three-row egress-control table into §0 or into an early 'Controls at a glance' block, or at minimum add a parenthetical gloss at first use: 'before Q-0 (the synthetic-only pre-ratification egress proxy, §2.3) existed.'

findings.title: Arithmetic in §2.5 does not reproduce from the stated formulas — the reader cannot verify the budget
findings.detail: The document invites verification by giving formulas and then a worked total, but the worked total does not follow. With R = 34.0022: cold_load = 0.5R = 17.001 → 17.01 ✓; runtime_qualification = 17.01 ✓; warm_authoring = 5R = 170.011 → 170.02 ✓; but max_in_flight_turn = max(0.5R, ((1620+120)/3600)R, ((90+120)/3600)R) = max(17.00, 16.43, 1.98) = 17.00 → 17.01 ✓. charge_reserve = 6×1.3707 + ((60+120)/3600)×34.0022 + 10 = 8.224 + 1.700 + 10 = 19.92, stated as 19.93 (rounding up per term, plausible). Sum = 240.98 ✓. But then 'operational contingency is USD 24.10' = 0.10 × 240.98 = 24.098 ✓, and cold_restart_contingency = cold_load + runtime_qualification = 34.02 ✓. Total 240.98 + 24.10 + 34.02 = 299.10 ✓. This actually checks out — but only after ~15 minutes of manual work, because the terms are defined in one bulleted list, the values appear in a separate paragraph, and the substitution steps are omitted. Worse, the separately-stated rate-ceiling inequality `1.10 * (6R + max(...) + 6S + ((60+D)/3600)R + 10) + R <= A` is a *different* expression from the sum of the bulleted terms (it folds cold_load+runtime_qualification into a single trailing `+ R` and uses `6R` where the list says `5R` warm + `0.5R` cold + `0.5R` qual), and no note explains the algebraic identity.
findings.evidence: Bulleted terms: `cold_load = 0.5R`, `runtime_qualification = 0.5R`, `warm_authoring = 5R`. Rate-ceiling inequality: `1.10 * (6R + max(...) + 6S + ((60+D)/3600)R + 10) + R <= A`. The `6R` and the trailing `+ R` are unexplained recombinations of `0.5R + 0.5R + 5R` and `cold_restart_contingency`.
findings.recommendation: Show the substitution explicitly (a small table: term, formula, R-substituted value, rounded value, running total). Add one sentence deriving the rate-ceiling inequality from the term list, or restate it using the same named terms.

findings.title: The 30-second observer hold and 90-second sentinel staleness limits are stated but their interaction with the 27-minute turn timeout and 870-second checkpoint cycle is never reconciled
findings.detail: Four independent timers govern the run: 30s observer hold, 90s sentinel staleness, 300/60/120/30/360s checkpoint phases summing to 870s, and 1620s turn timeout. The document asserts each individually but never states which wins when they collide. Concretely: what happens if the checkpoint watchdog reaches second 300 (revoke new tool release) while an observer hold is at second 25 of 30, and the sentinel simultaneously sees a 91-second-stale monitor sample? Three different terminal sequences are described in three different places (§2.1 observer stall → `UNFUNDED_BY_OBSERVER_STALL`; §2.1 checkpoint phase failure → 'terminates the route no later than second 870'; §2.5 sentinel → 'starts the same terminal sequence'). A reader cannot determine the resulting error code or whether the last checkpoint is admissible.
findings.evidence: §2.1: 'A hold has a 30-second maximum. Timeout or observer volume exhaustion discards the held body, cancels the model turn... emits UNFUNDED_BY_OBSERVER_STALL.' §2.1: 'Failure of any phase kills the gated source writer... and terminates the route no later than second 870.' §2.5: 'A second sentinel... requires a fresh monitor sample at least every 90 seconds; otherwise it denies new traffic and invokes stop/destroy.' No precedence rule.
findings.recommendation: Add a short precedence/ordering statement: which timer's terminal sequence executes first, whether codes compose (e.g. both appended) or one supersedes, and what the checkpoint disposition is in each case. A worked example of one concurrent-timer scenario would be worth more than another paragraph of prose.

findings.title: 'The bundle members are the rows of this table; its derived row count is nine' hard-codes a magic number that must be maintained by hand
findings.detail: The bundle-root preimage requires a decimal count that 'must also equal the row count derived from the bundle-member table.' The prose asserts the count is nine. A reader adding or removing a supplemental artifact in a future amendment must remember to update this English sentence, the table, the preimage, and any downstream '`nine`-member' references (which appear at least twice more: 'freezes all nine' and 'the complete nine-member effective authority bundle'). This is exactly the kind of manually-synchronized constant that silently drifts.
findings.evidence: 'The bundle members are the rows of this table; its derived row count is nine' / 'freezes all nine in a read-only, content-addressed candidate bundle' / 'exposes the complete nine-member effective authority bundle to the named processor'.
findings.recommendation: State the count once, normatively, and reference it symbolically elsewhere ('the bundle-member count declared above'). Or remove the literal from prose entirely and let the table be the sole source, with the materializer required to derive it.

findings.title: The link-census regex will match Markdown links inside the very blockquotes it must not interpret, and this is asserted rather than analyzed
findings.detail: The document requires scanning 'the raw UTF-8 of every bundle document for every non-overlapping occurrence of the literal regular expression `]\(([^)#]+\.md)(?:#[^)]+)?\)`, including occurrences inside code fences or inline code'. Bundle member `spec/amendment-001-rust-vast.md` (this file) contains quoted blocks that become part of other artifacts, and also contains at least one real link: `[glossary.md](glossary.md)`. The document says paths in backticks don't match — true — but it never addresses that a link appearing inside a `>`-quoted *new block* will be scanned twice: once in the amendment's own bytes and once in the materialized target artifact. Whether that is intended, harmless, or a duplicate-census hazard is left to the reader to reason out. The document also never states what happens if a bundle member contains a `.md` link to a file that exists under `spec/` but is *not* a bundle member — it says 'require the target to remain under `spec/` and be a bundle member' but assigns no error code to that failure.
findings.evidence: 'Both materializers independently scan the raw UTF-8 of every bundle document... including occurrences inside code fences or inline code; there is no CommonMark interpretation step.' and 'They resolve the captured path against the referring document and require the target to remain under `spec/` and be a bundle member.' No failure code is named for a non-member `spec/` target.
findings.recommendation: Name the failure code for a link to a non-member `spec/` path. State explicitly whether the amendment's own quoted blocks are scanned in addition to the materialized targets, and whether duplicate census rows are expected. A two-line worked example of the census output would resolve both.

findings.title: Sentence length and clause density make normative requirements unparseable on first read
findings.detail: Many requirements are single sentences of 60-100+ words chaining five or more independent obligations with semicolons and 'plus'. A reader trying to build a checklist must re-parse each one. This is not stylistic nitpicking: in a document whose entire purpose is that a Validator executes it exactly, an obligation buried mid-clause in an 80-word sentence is an obligation that will be missed.
findings.evidence: Example: 'It receives no Personal or Company root/socket, Tester/Detector/Oracle path, unrelated repository, general user home, cloud credential, or direct IP network capability beyond one run-specific loopback admission-proxy listener whose address, port, executable identity, and configuration digest are bound.' Example: the G-1 'Required evidence' cell, ~130 words, containing at least nine distinct deliverables. Example: 'a Personal marker must never reach any shared byte; an unauthorized Company marker must never reach `.kin/`; and a Codebase event must never mint/supersede a Company fact.'  (this one is good — it is a list; most are not).
findings.recommendation: Convert every enumeration of three or more obligations into a bulleted list. This is mechanical, changes no semantics, and would likely cut perceived complexity in half.

findings.title: Two operations (O-01, O-02) share the same containing heading with no stated disambiguation for the reader
findings.detail: The operation/heading table shows O-01 and O-02 both under `## 1. One protocol, three bounded products`, and O-09/O-10/O-11 all under `### P-10 — material brownfield outcome improvement`. The rules require each *source block* to occur exactly once, which resolves the mechanical ambiguity — but a reader scanning the table sees an apparent collision and must reconstruct why it's fine. Nothing in the table or its surrounding text says 'multiple operations may share a heading; uniqueness is enforced at the source-block level.'
findings.evidence: Table rows: O-01 and O-02 both `## 1. One protocol, three bounded products`; O-09, O-10, O-11 all `### P-10 — material brownfield outcome improvement`.
findings.recommendation: Add one sentence under the table: 'Multiple operations may name the same heading; uniqueness is enforced per source block, not per heading.'

findings.title: Status line says 'no Coder dispatch permitted from these bytes' but the mechanism enforcing that is never named
findings.detail: The header declares 'Status: candidate; not authority; no Coder dispatch permitted from these bytes'. A reader naturally asks: what stops it? The answer is scattered — G-1 gates dispatch, and 'reading a superseded base file or rerunning the overlay inside an author lane is AUTHORITY_MISMATCH' — but the status line itself is an unenforced assertion, and a reader who only skims the header may treat it as decorative.
findings.evidence: 'Status: **candidate; not authority; no Coder dispatch permitted from these bytes**' with no cross-reference.
findings.recommendation: Append a cross-reference: '(enforced by G-1 and G-5; see §8)'.

findings.title: Section 0 is titled 'Stakes' but contains a hard normative prohibition and a permanent host disqualification
findings.detail: A reader skimming section titles will read 'Stakes' as risk framing and may skip it. It in fact contains one of the strongest operational rules in the document ('no byte sourced from the Guildhall repository... may reach the Vast host before this amendment is exactly ratified') and the permanent disqualification of instance `50012413`. Burying a binding prohibition under a soft title is a navigation hazard.
findings.evidence: §0 'Stakes' contains: 'Therefore public model staging may precede ratification, but no byte sourced from the Guildhall repository... may reach the Vast host before this amendment is exactly ratified.' and 'instance `50012413` is permanently ineligible for repository-bearing traffic and must be destroyed before a replacement is staged.'
findings.recommendation: Retitle to '0. Stakes and pre-ratification prohibitions', or split the normative prohibition into its own numbered subsection so it is addressable and unskippable.

findings.title: Referenced evidence files are cited by path without digests, unlike the two supplemental artifacts which are digest-bound
findings.detail: The document digest-binds `spec/glossary.md` and `spec/leak-runbook.md` and explains why. But it cites at least seven `evidence/factory-run/*.md` files as load-bearing (feasibility survey, toolchain observation, qualification receipt, risk observation, SSH source observation, review-window status, account-control observation) with only one — `pre-outcome-null-census-001.md` — carrying a SHA-256. A reader has no way to know whether the others are authority, mutable observations, or something in between, and the doc's own principle ('a digest mismatch is `AUTHORITY_MISMATCH`') suggests undigested references are unverifiable by construction.
findings.evidence: Digest-bound: `pre-outcome-null-census-001.md` at `0106b366...`. Not digest-bound but cited as evidence: `rust-boundary-feasibility-002.md`, `rust-toolchain-observation-001.md`, `vast-glm53-qualification-001.md`, `vast-instance-risk-observation-003.md`, `vast-ssh-source-observation-001.md`, `vast-review-window-status-004.md`, `vast-account-control-observation-001.md`.
findings.recommendation: State once, explicitly, that `evidence/factory-run/*` are non-authoritative operational observations outside the bundle and are deliberately not digest-bound — or digest-bind them. Right now the asymmetry reads as an oversight.

persona_reports.summary: **Summary.** The specification is internally rigorous and the arithmetic I could check reproduces correctly, but as a *document to navigate* it fails the "no guide needed" bar decisively: it opens with its most mechanical content before saying what it does, points readers to a "checklist" that isn't one, uses undefined actor names (Agy, Codex, Claude, kin) as load-bearing terms, and forward-references Q-0/Q-1/Q-2 three sections before defining them. The two most actionable fixes are cheap and semantics-preserving — add an actors table and a real ordered procedure — and would remove most of the friction. The genuine correctness concerns I found are narrower: `AUTHORITY_MISMATCH` is overloaded across nine unrelated conditions with no sub-codes, `UNFUNDED_BY_RECONCILIATION_STALL` is missing from the §8 code table while `INVALID_PLAN` has no emission site, and the four concurrent timers (30s/90s/870s/1620s) have no stated precedence when they collide.

findings.title: Landlock cannot enforce the claimed network confinement; no kernel/ABI floor is pinned
findings.detail: The amendment repeatedly presents the Coder sandbox's network isolation as kernel-enforced and names Landlock as the Linux mechanism ('bubblewrap plus Landlock', 'An untrusted model tool call cannot widen these kernel-enforced capabilities', 'Sole-egress is an invariant: the Coder sandbox has no other network namespace, socket, inherited tunnel descriptor, DNS path'). Landlock ABI v1 (kernel 5.13) through v3 (6.2) are filesystem-only. Network restriction (TCP bind/connect) arrives only in Landlock ABI v4 / kernel 6.7, and even then covers neither UDP, nor raw sockets, nor AF_UNIX. Actual sole-egress must come from an empty network namespace plus seccomp, which the document mentions only in passing and never specifies as the enforcing mechanism. No minimum kernel version, Landlock ABI level, or seccomp filter is pinned anywhere, despite every other input being digest-pinned. This is the stated 'confidentiality root' of Q-1 resting on a mechanism that cannot deliver it. The same omission undermines 'landlock 0.4.7' being cited as feasibility evidence for the Linux path: the crate version does not determine the runtime ABI the kernel grants, and Landlock is best-effort by design (a kernel supporting only v1 silently grants less unless the program hard-requires a level).
findings.evidence: §2.1: 'bubblewrap plus Landlock on a replacement Linux workstation'; 'Sole-egress is an invariant: the Coder sandbox has no other network namespace, socket, inherited tunnel descriptor, DNS path, or provider-side agent'; 'An untrusted model tool call cannot widen these kernel-enforced capabilities'; §2.1 feasibility: 'safe public APIs in nix 0.31.2, rustix 1.1.4, and landlock 0.4.7 for the Linux path'; G-9 row: 'Linux hard-requirement external-classifier confinement'.
findings.recommendation: Pin a minimum kernel version and required Landlock ABI level as run inputs alongside the image/model digests. State explicitly that network sole-egress is enforced by an unshared network namespace containing only `lo` plus the single admission-proxy listener, with seccomp denying socket families outside AF_UNIX/AF_INET-to-loopback; name Landlock as the filesystem control only. Add a G-4 negative probe that attempts AF_INET, AF_INET6, AF_PACKET, AF_NETLINK, and UDP/DNS from inside the Coder sandbox and requires denial for each, since a Landlock-only configuration would pass a TCP-connect probe on ABI v4 while leaving UDP open.

findings.title: Checkpoint refs are isolated but checkpoint objects are not: the Coder shares the Git object database
findings.detail: The watchdog is specified to 'use a private temporary Git index to create a content-addressed checkpoint ref outside the Coder sandbox without staging or rewriting the Coder's index.' GIT_INDEX_FILE redirection isolates the index, and placing the ref outside the sandbox isolates the ref. Neither isolates the *objects*. The tree and blob objects the checkpoint references must be written into an object database, and the amendment simultaneously requires 'The Coder commits every independently coherent slice' — so the Coder holds write capability to that same ODB. Consequences: (a) a `git gc`, `git prune`, or repack initiated from the Coder lane can remove or rewrite objects the checkpoint ref depends on, since the ref is outside the repository's ref namespace and therefore invisible to reachability analysis; (b) the doc's integrity control is a double read of the journal head plus two consecutive worktree tree-digest computations, which detects worktree mutation but not ODB corruption or object removal after admission. The stated property that 'The last prior admitted checkpoint remains the only recoverable source state' therefore does not hold under a Coder-side ODB operation, and the recovery story in §2.2 and failure mode 6 depends on it.
findings.evidence: §2.2 checkpoint block: 'uses a private temporary Git index to create a content-addressed checkpoint ref outside the Coder sandbox without staging or rewriting the Coder's index, reads the journal head again, and computes the source-worktree tree digest twice consecutively'; and 'The Coder commits every independently coherent slice'; §2.2 prior-art block: 'Validator-custodied, mode-0700 content-addressed manifest outside author lanes'.
findings.recommendation: Redirect checkpoint object writes with GIT_OBJECT_DIRECTORY to a Validator-owned object store outside the Coder's write policy (with the Coder's ODB as a read-only alternate), so no Coder-side operation can affect checkpoint durability. Alternatively, state that the checkpoint is a full content-addressed copy into Validator-owned storage rather than a Git ref. Either way, add a G-4 drill that runs `git gc --prune=now --aggressive` and a `git reflog expire` from the Coder lane after an admitted checkpoint and proves the checkpoint remains fully resolvable.

findings.title: Single-false-positive INVALID_HARNESS is an unreachable operating point at the stated candidate volume
findings.detail: The egress detector qualifies on zero false positives across 500 decoys, and the amendment correctly refuses to convert that into a union bound. But the disposition rule is absolute: 'A mechanically confirmed false positive or unresolved scanner/Detector disagreement is INVALID_HARNESS.' With M_egress at the stated structural minimum of 660 candidates — and the document says the powered census is expected to exceed that 'potentially substantially' — a single false positive invalidates the entire measurement. If the true field FPR is anywhere near the calibration ceiling the amendment itself computes (Wilson upper 0.0076, which I verify as correct: center (0+z^2/2)/(n+z^2)=1.9208/503.84=0.003812, half-width (z/(n+z^2))*sqrt(z^2/4)=0.003812, upper=0.00762), then P(at least one FP over 660 candidates) = 1-(1-0.0076)^660 ~ 99.4%. The amendment is thus structured so that its most likely terminal state is INVALID_HARNESS for reasons entirely unrelated to Product quality, after the full G-10 measurement spend has been committed. The document is admirably honest that 500 decoys prove nothing about 660 real candidates, but it does not follow that honesty through to the disposition rule that depends on it.
findings.evidence: §2.6 candidate-egress block: 'Qualification requires zero observed false positives across at least 500 frozen, stratified, difficulty-matched decoys'; 'At 500 zero-positive decoys the two-sided 95% Wilson upper bound for that frozen decoy population is approximately 0.0076; this is reported as a calibration statistic only'; 'The statistic is not divided by M_egress, is not a familywise guarantee, and does not pretend that 500 establishes a one-percent union bound over the structural minimum of 660'; and 'A mechanically confirmed false positive or unresolved scanner/Detector disagreement is INVALID_HARNESS, not a comparator-only zero that can buy a lift margin.'
findings.recommendation: Either (a) scale the decoy corpus so the qualification bound is meaningful relative to M_egress — a zero-positive requirement over ~3*M_egress decoys gives a 95% upper bound near 1/M_egress — and price that in the G-10 plan; or (b) preregister a bounded false-positive budget: each confirmed FP scores its cell zero AND is reported per-arm under blinding, with INVALID_HARNESS triggered only when the observed FP count exceeds a preregistered threshold, or when the per-arm FP distribution is non-uniform beyond a preregistered test. Option (b) preserves the stated anti-gaming property (arm-dependent FPs cannot manufacture lift) while making the harness survivable. The current text's own justification for the absolute rule — that FPs could buy a lift margin — is satisfied by the blinded per-arm reporting plus a uniformity test, not only by total invalidation.

findings.title: G-9 requires the macOS artifact both to omit every classifier identifier string and to emit a classifier-specific error for classifier fields
findings.detail: Two G-9 obligations are jointly unsatisfiable as written. The amendment requires the macOS binary to contain 'no external-classifier module, command, configuration variant, launcher, or identifier string' and requires G-9 to prove this by 'artifact hash/symbol/string' inspection. It simultaneously requires that 'The closed macOS schema rejects a manifest or invocation containing an unknown Linux-only classifier field or command with UNSUPPORTED_UNPROVEN_PLATFORM before classifier bytes, process creation, or network access.' To emit a field-specific disposition for a specific unknown key, the binary must be able to distinguish that key from any other unknown key, which requires carrying the key name (or a hash of it, which is still an identifier by the stated symbol/string test). A genuinely closed schema with no classifier knowledge produces a generic unknown-field rejection and cannot name UNSUPPORTED_UNPROVEN_PLATFORM specifically. The amendment even gestures at this tension ('the shared error code does not introduce the omitted surface') without resolving it. As written G-9 has a branch that must fail.
findings.evidence: §2.1: 'Target-specific compilation must omit the external-classifier module, command, configuration variant, and launcher from the macOS artifact. The closed macOS schema rejects a manifest or invocation containing an unknown Linux-only classifier field or command with UNSUPPORTED_UNPROVEN_PLATFORM'; G-9 row: 'macOS artifact hash/symbol/string/schema proof that the external-classifier module/command/configuration/launcher is omitted plus hostile configuration/launch denial'; failure mode 17: 'contains an external-classifier module, command, configuration variant, launcher, identifier string, or accepts a hostile Linux-only classifier invocation.'
findings.recommendation: Pick one and state it. Cleanest: the macOS artifact rejects *any* unknown manifest key or subcommand with a single generic closed-schema error, and UNSUPPORTED_UNPROVEN_PLATFORM is redefined as the disposition class for that rejection rather than a classifier-aware code. Then the string-omission proof and the denial proof are compatible, and G-9's negative test becomes 'no unknown key of any kind is accepted' — which is strictly stronger than classifier-specific denial and does not leak the omitted surface. Update the terminal-code table's UNSUPPORTED_UNPROVEN_PLATFORM row accordingly.

findings.title: Observer body-digest custody assumes HTTP request framing the wrapper is never specified to parse
findings.detail: The custody chain's authority claim is that 'The observer is authority for the exact post-admission HTTP body digest/count/byte-count list that reached SSH' and 'The wrapper buffers and hashes the exact body it will forward.' This presumes each 'body' is unambiguously delimited on the wire. Over a persistent HTTP/1.1 connection through an SSH-forwarded port, delimiting a body requires protocol-aware parsing of Content-Length or chunked Transfer-Encoding; a byte-oriented relay cannot establish where one body ends and the next begins, and pipelined or chunked requests break the one-token-per-body accounting entirely. The amendment never states that the observer/wrapper is a terminating, protocol-aware HTTP proxy that buffers each complete request before forwarding. Two dependent claims inherit the gap: the one-use HMAC over (run_generation, sequence, predecessor_digest, body_sha256, body_byte_count) cannot bind a body whose extent is undetermined, and 'Application retries are new counted custody events, while transport retransmission is not a second HTTP body' requires exactly this layer distinction. Relatedly, Codex-style harnesses typically use streaming responses; buffering the full request before the token is spent forecloses request-side streaming, which should be stated as a constraint rather than discovered at G-4.
findings.evidence: §2.1: 'The observer is authority for the exact post-admission HTTP body digest/count/byte-count list that reached SSH. It fsyncs and acknowledges the next chained sequence before releasing that body.'; 'The wrapper buffers and hashes the exact body it will forward, verifies every committed field, atomically spends the sequence, and refuses substitution or replay.'; 'Independent SSH connection/byte counters are diagnostic cross-checks, not alternative body authority.'
findings.recommendation: Specify the observer and SSH wrapper as terminating HTTP/1.1 proxies that fully buffer each request, reject Transfer-Encoding: chunked and pipelining, require Content-Length, and open a fresh upstream request per admitted body. Add G-4 positive controls that attempt a chunked request, a pipelined pair on one connection, and an oversized body, and require rejection of each. State explicitly that request-side streaming is unsupported in this generation.

findings.title: The stratified P-10 endpoints, not the aggregate ones, will drive N — and the document does not say so
findings.detail: The amended co-primary set is roughly sixteen endpoints under an intersection-union test. IUT is applied correctly (no alpha adjustment needed; the conjunction is conservative), and the amendment is right that no favorable endpoint can be selected from a family. But the power consequence is understated. Most endpoints share the full-system arm and are strongly positively correlated, which the Gaussian-copula model can exploit. Two endpoints do not: 'paired superiority over codebase-only on Company-unique tasks' and 'company-only on Codebase-unique tasks' are estimated on *disjoint task strata*, are near-independent of each other, and each uses only a fraction of the task census. At the stated eight-task measurement minimum split across two strata with three seeds, a paired 0.10 superiority bound would rest on roughly a dozen cells per stratum — nowhere near 80% marginal power at any plausible variance. The authorization-restricted stratum adds a third disjoint subset carrying three more conjuncts at 0.90/0.15/±0.05. The document says 'the post-amendment power program is expected to exceed [660 cells], potentially substantially,' which is true but does not identify *which* endpoints bind. A founder reading this to decide whether to prepay the G-10 ceiling cannot see that the cost driver is stratum-level power, not the newly added aggregate conjuncts.
findings.evidence: New V-10 paragraph: 'Co-primary endpoints are absolute full-system composite quality 0.90; absolute full-system held-out functional quality 0.90; ... paired superiority over codebase-only on Company-unique tasks and company-only on Codebase-unique tasks 0.10; and authorization-restricted-stratum quality/lift/equivalence at the same 0.90/0.15/±0.05 bounds.'; §2.5: 'the minimum eight-task measurement x eleven arms x three seeds = 264 more'; 'the post-amendment power program is expected to exceed it, potentially substantially.'
findings.recommendation: Require the G-10 pilot report to present per-endpoint marginal power at the selected N, explicitly separating aggregate endpoints from stratum-restricted ones, and to report the minimum per-stratum cell count each 0.10 bound rests on. Require the pilot plan to state the binding endpoint. Also add a preregistered minimum tasks-per-stratum so the power program cannot satisfy the joint criterion by drawing a task census that starves one stratum.

findings.title: G-3 consumes the sole restart allowance, leaving zero preemption tolerance for the entire funded window
findings.detail: The budget reserves exactly one cold restart. §2.5 then states 'G-3 consumes it to replace the disqualified pre-ratification host, so no post-disclosure restart remains,' and §2.2 states 'A second preemption terminates this funded Coder attempt.' Since G-3's rehost is mandatory, not contingent, the route enters its five protected warm hours with zero tolerance for any host, provider, or network failure. The amendment's own risk evidence undercuts the implied safety: it records reliability2=0.9992037 while correctly warning this 'is evidence against bid-price preemption, not an SLA or a five-hour completion probability; host/provider/network failure remains possible.' Combined with the observation that the *previous* route 'terminated seven times without an admissible Coder commit,' the design commits an irreversible specification disclosure to a single-attempt, zero-margin route. This is a legitimate founder choice, but it is presented as an incidental accounting consequence in §2.5 rather than as a first-order risk in §0 Stakes or §5 Assumptions, where the founder ratification decision is framed.
findings.evidence: §2.5: 'At current rates and the proposed USD 400 ceiling reserves one cold restart; G-3 consumes it to replace the disqualified pre-ratification host, so no post-disclosure restart remains.'; §2.2: 'A second preemption terminates this funded Coder attempt, destroys any surviving instance, and retains only the last local quiescent checkpoint as unadmitted prior art.'; §0: 'no calibrated completion probability'; §1: 'terminated seven times without an admissible Coder commit.'
findings.recommendation: Promote this to §0 and to §5 assumption 3 in explicit terms: after the mandatory G-3 rehost, a single preemption ends the attempt with the specification bundle already disclosed and no restart funding. State it in the founder ratification receipt requirement alongside the existing 'irreversible specification disclosure ... with one cold-restart allowance' language, which currently reads as though the allowance survives ratification. If the founder wants any margin, the correct lever is a second restart allowance priced into C, not a relaxed gate.

findings.title: The headline budget figure USD 240.98 is not reproducible from the stated terms
findings.detail: At R = 34.0022/hr and S = 1.3707/hr the five terms are: cold_load 0.5R = 17.0011; runtime_qualification 0.5R = 17.0011; warm_authoring 5R = 170.0110; max_in_flight_turn = max(17.0011, ((1620+120)/3600)*R = 16.4344, ((90+120)/3600)*R = 1.9835) = 17.0011; charge_reserve = 6*1.3707 + ((60+120)/3600)*34.0022 + 10 = 8.2242 + 1.7001 + 10 = 19.9243. Unrounded sum = 240.9386 (240.94 to cents). Rounded up per term as the text directs (17.01 + 17.01 + 170.02 + 17.01 + 19.93) = 241.00. The stated 240.98 matches neither convention. Downstream figures are internally consistent with 240.98 (0.10 * 240.9386 = 24.094 -> 24.10 matches the unrounded base; 240.98 + 24.10 + 34.02 = 299.10 as stated), so the error is confined to the one subtotal. Materially this is ~USD 0.06 against a USD 2.00 uncertainty floor and a 10% contingency, so it is not a safety defect. It is an auditability defect in a document whose authority rests on exact reproducible arithmetic and which states 'Cent rounding is presentation only and contributes no claimed safety margin.' A peer verifying the numbers finds one that does not reproduce, which weakens confidence in the others. For the record, the rate-ceiling inequality does check out: solving 1.10*(6.55R + 18.2242) + R <= 342.0825 gives R <= 39.24, consistent with the stated illustrative 39.25.
findings.evidence: §2.5: 'At the recorded rates those terms are USD 17.01 + 17.01 + 170.02 + 17.01 + 19.93 = USD 240.98 (rounded upward per term), operational contingency is USD 24.10, and one cold-restart contingency is USD 34.02: USD 299.10 total.'
findings.recommendation: State one rounding convention and apply it. Recommend: compute all terms unrounded, sum, then round the sum upward once — giving 240.94, contingency 24.10, restart 34.02, total 299.06. Present the per-term values as unrounded to four decimals so a reviewer can reproduce them, and correct the displayed sum. Alternatively adopt round-up-per-term consistently and state 241.00 / 299.12.

findings.title: The $400 you're arguing about is a rounding error next to the $50k+ V-10 measurement you haven't priced
findings.detail: Section 2.5 admits the structural floor: 660 coding cells and 1,320 two-grader passes, and explicitly says the post-amendment power program 'is expected to exceed it, potentially substantially.' Each coding cell is an agentic coding run on a brownfield repo — realistically dollars to tens of dollars each, plus two grader passes each. That is plausibly five figures before you've bought a single hour of proof value. Meanwhile this document spends thousands of words on a $2.00 uncertainty floor, a 60-second poll interval, and a 30-second observer hold. The precision is inversely proportional to the dollar magnitude. You are optimizing the cheap thing to three decimal places and deferring the expensive thing to 'G-10 will tell us.'
findings.evidence: 'twelve excluded pilot tasks x eleven arms x three seeds = 396 coding cells, and the minimum eight-task measurement x eleven arms x three seeds = 264 more, for at least 660 coding cells and 1,320 two-grader measurement/pilot score passes' ... 'It is not a cost estimate and is not funded by the proposed USD 400.'
findings.recommendation: Before spending the $400, do a 30-minute back-of-envelope on the V-10 census at three price points (cheap/mid/frontier coding model). If the honest answer is $30k and you don't have $30k, then the Rust build is a $400 down payment on a proof you cannot afford to finish, and you should know that today rather than after G-6. Put that number in section 2.5 as a range with stated assumptions, not as 'the pilot will tell us.'

findings.title: Five hours of $34/hr GPU with a 5-minute human heartbeat requirement is not a system, it's a vigil
findings.detail: Section 2.5 requires a local operator heartbeat every five minutes, a 90-second sentinel staleness limit, a 60-second poll, a 30-second observer hold, and a 27-minute in-flight cancel. Losing the heartbeat closes admission. The document says 'No human must stay awake merely to keep a safe default alive' — but the safe default here is stopping, which means the human must stay awake to keep the *expensive thing running*. You have a five-hour, one-restart, non-replenishable budget window. If you step away for six minutes at hour three, admission closes and you burn part of your remaining allocation restarting the clock. This fails the 3am test not because it's dangerous, but because it is a five-hour attention-tether with irrecoverable cost on lapse.
findings.evidence: 'The monitor also requires a local operator heartbeat every five minutes. Loss of the heartbeat closes new-turn/tool admission' combined with 'Every restart still must make the live inequality true' and 'the one allowed replacement cold-load/qualification'.
findings.recommendation: Decide explicitly and write it down: is this a supervised five-hour session where you sit at the desk, or is it unattended? If supervised, say so and schedule it as such (not at 11pm after a long day). If unattended, the heartbeat requirement is wrong and needs a different safe-default design. Do not discover which one it is at hour 2.5.

findings.title: Every enumerated failure mode terminates the route; none of them recover it — and there is exactly one restart, already spent
findings.detail: Section 3 lists seventeen failure modes. Count the dispositions: destroy, stop, block, terminate, UNFUNDED, incomplete. Not one of them says 'retry and continue.' Meanwhile section 2.5 states the single cold-restart allowance is consumed by G-3 to replace instance 50012413 'so no post-disclosure restart remains.' So the operational reality is: seventeen distinct ways to lose, zero ways to recover, and the spare tire is already used before you leave the driveway. Any one of parser drift, observer fsync stall, provider preemption, rate increase, unattributed balance delta, or destroy-receipt timeout ends the attempt with sunk cost and no admissible commit.
findings.evidence: 'G-3 consumes it to replace the disqualified pre-ratification host, so no post-disclosure restart remains.' Cross-referenced against failure modes 1, 2, 3, 5, 6, 7, 14, 15, 16 — each of which independently terminates.
findings.recommendation: Compute the honest joint survival probability. Even at 95% per independent hazard across nine live hazards you're under 65%. Either fund a second restart allowance before starting, or state plainly in section 0 that the expected outcome of this $400 is an incomplete attempt and that you are buying information, not a build. The current framing lets you believe you're buying a build.

findings.title: Two independently-authored materializers, a 500-decoy detector corpus, and a fresh Tester are all unbuilt prerequisites with no cost line
findings.detail: G-1 requires 'two structurally separate equal plans/bundles' plus a frozen adversarial parser corpus. G-8/V-10 requires 'at least 500 frozen, stratified, difficulty-matched decoys spanning every scanner-visible encoding, candidate format, boundary position, and benign provenance class.' G-7 requires a fresh Claude Tester deriving the complete V-1 through V-10 instrument from scratch. None of these exist. None of them are in any budget. The $400 is for the Vast host. These are weeks of your own unpaid labor, and the amendment presents them as gate rows rather than as the dominant cost of the project.
findings.evidence: Section 8 G-1 row and the V-10 egress insert: 'The exact M_egress, decoy count, construction cost, difficulty strata, draw, and named Tester/Detector-Reviewer ownership freeze with the detector and are priced in the separately funded G-10 plan.'
findings.recommendation: Write down the estimated person-days for: second materializer, parser corpus, 500-decoy stratified corpus, fresh Tester instrument, Detector Reviewer pass. Sum it. If that number is larger than your available calendar before the thing you're actually trying to prove matters, you need to know now.

findings.title: UNCONFIRMED_DESTROY creates an unbounded liability that your $400 local ceiling explicitly does not cap
findings.detail: The amendment is admirably honest that 'C is only a local authorization ceiling and is not represented as a cap on provider liability.' But then it defines the failure path: if destroy doesn't return a trustworthy receipt inside the accounting floor, 'the greatest observed running rate times elapsed time accumulates without bound.' At $34/hr, an unnoticed live instance costs $816/day. Your defense is credit-only billing with autobill disabled — which caps actual loss at your balance, but that balance is currently ~$343 and you'd lose all of it plus whatever the incident costs in attention. This is a real, quantified, plausible way to lose the entire remaining credit to a stuck API response.
findings.evidence: 'From the attempted-destroy timestamp until a trustworthy terminal provider observation, the greatest observed running rate times elapsed time accumulates without bound in authorization_uncertainty' and 'C is only a local authorization ceiling'.
findings.recommendation: The credit-only/no-autobill observation in G-2 is doing more real financial work than the entire budget formula apparatus. Say so explicitly. Also: set a phone alarm for the destroy confirmation. The formal control is 'escalate until trustworthy terminal evidence'; the actual control is you noticing.

findings.title: The nine-member authority bundle — including account IDs, host bindings, and all control topology — is irreversibly disclosed to a marketplace host on the first request
findings.detail: Section 2.4 states the first repository-bearing request exposes the complete nine-member bundle 'including this amendment's account/host binding, control topology, timeout values, polling cadences, reserve formulas, and terminal conditions.' The amendment argues correctness doesn't depend on processor ignorance, which is correct as a security argument. But blast radius is not just security: you are permanently handing a third-party marketplace operator your Vast account number, your instance IDs, your complete operational playbook, and your budget ceilings. If any of this is embarrassing, competitively sensitive, or reusable against you, it is gone the moment the first request crosses. The document treats this as a ratification checkbox rather than as a decision with a named worst case.
findings.evidence: 'The first repository-bearing request exposes the complete nine-member effective authority bundle to the named processor, including this amendment's account/host binding, control topology, timeout values, polling cadences, reserve formulas, and terminal conditions.'
findings.recommendation: Ask yourself concretely: if this entire bundle appeared on a public forum tomorrow attributed to you, what is the worst consequence? If the answer is 'mild embarrassment,' fine — write that down and move on. If it includes 'account 413964 gets targeted' or 'a competitor learns the design,' redact what you can before ratification. The specification says provider access 'cannot be excluded' — believe it.

findings.title: Five hours is an allocation, not an estimate, and the document knows it — which means the most likely outcome is a partial build you cannot use
findings.detail: Section 2.5 is explicit: 'Five hours is a founder-authorized allocation only upon ratification, not a duration calibrated from prior complete Rust Guildhall runs; no completion probability is claimed.' The prior evidence point is that a 29-module, 9,378-line Python attempt failed seven times without an admissible commit. You are now asking a model to produce a complete P-1 through P-10 Rust implementation — with process isolation, Landlock, capability passing, SQLite services, content-addressed event stores — in eight 30-minute slots. And G-6 is all-or-nothing: 'one clean final Rust HEAD whose reachable Coder series maps every effective P-1 through P-10 obligation.' Partial work is explicitly 'unadmitted prior art' with a 30-day self-destruct.
findings.evidence: 'The Ollama route repeatedly replayed an approximately 200K-token context without reported cache hits, exhausted purchased usage, and terminated seven times without an admissible Coder commit.' vs. 'The proposed ceiling therefore funds at most five protected warm Coder hours in total.'
findings.recommendation: The seven prior failures are your only calibration data and they all say 'not enough.' Either accept that this run's realistic product is a VOI plan plus partial code and budget accordingly, or change the shape of the work (smaller Coder scope per generation, multiple funded generations) rather than betting five hours on an all-or-nothing G-6. The amendment rejects a vertical slice in section 7.7 on principle; principle does not buy GPU hours.

findings.title: The 870-second checkpoint budget assumes a 1 GiB / 20,000-path tree; a Rust workspace's target/ directory blows past that in one build
findings.detail: G-4 qualifies exactly 20,000 paths and 1,073,741,824 content bytes, and mutations that would exceed either cap are rejected with CHECKPOINT_CAPACITY_EXCEEDED, which requires a new ratified amendment to expand. The document says 'Longer builds write only disposable build/cache roots and cannot modify source' — so target/ is presumably excluded. But a vendored Rust dependency tree for nix + rustix + landlock + tokio-class dependencies is easily tens of thousands of files. If vendored sources land inside the checkpointed source tree, you hit the cap mid-run and the disposition is 'terminate the route.' That is a project-ending outcome from a directory listing.
findings.evidence: 'G-4 qualifies the exact maximum live-source envelope of 20,000 paths and 1,073,741,824 content bytes' and 'Expanding either cap requires a new founder/Validator-ratified amendment and fresh G-4 qualification'.
findings.recommendation: Before G-4, actually count: cargo vendor a representative dependency set and count paths and bytes. If it's near 20,000, raise the cap now while it's a paragraph edit rather than a mid-run amendment ceremony you cannot afford.

findings.title: Watchdog phase sum is 870s but the checkpoint interval is 300s — overlapping cycles are undefined
findings.detail: The fixed schedule sets checkpoint_start_interval_seconds = 300 and a total phase budget of 870 seconds, with the requirement that the watchdog 'completes or terminates each checkpoint cycle before fifteen minutes have elapsed from the prior admitted checkpoint.' If a cycle legitimately consumes 870 seconds, the next two 300-second start triggers fire during it. The document does not say whether those are suppressed, queued, or count as missed deadlines triggering termination. At 3am, with $34/hr burning, 'the watchdog terminated the route and I don't know if it was correct' is exactly the wrong ambiguity to have.
findings.evidence: 'checkpoint_start_interval_seconds = 300 ... their sum is 870 seconds' and 'Failure of any phase kills the gated source writer ... and terminates the route no later than second 870.'
findings.recommendation: State the interaction explicitly: start triggers are suppressed while a cycle is in flight, and the 15-minute deadline runs from the last *admitted* checkpoint. One sentence. Add a G-4 drill that runs a deliberately slow 870-second cycle and proves no spurious termination.

findings.title: The founder is the standing security custodian with no successor, indefinitely
findings.detail: Section 2.4: 'Until delegated in a signed run record accepted by the named successor, the founder is the standing post-run security custodian and owns disclosure response and the authoritative rightsholder roster... silence or an expired/unreachable delegate leaves ownership with the founder.' Combined with 'The memory is retained for the life of the proof claim,' this is a permanent, non-delegable, single-person obligation created by ratifying an amendment. If you are hit by a bus, or simply stop caring about this project in eighteen months, the rightsholders in the auxiliary corpus have a custodian who does not respond.
findings.evidence: 'before a Company steward exists the founder remains responsible' and 'The memory is retained for the life of the proof claim; correction is a new linked record, never an overwrite.'
findings.recommendation: This is fine for a solo project you intend to maintain. It is not fine if you plan to hand this off or abandon it. Before soliciting the G-8 named-human rights grant, decide what happens to those people's data if you disappear, and tell them. That is a conversation with a human, not a clause.

findings.title: Vendor lock-in to a single Vast instance/machine/host with no equivalence rule
findings.detail: The design pins one 8xH200 host and states 'A replacement must retain GPU model/count, exact image/model/configuration digests, and rerun every capacity, parser, tunnel, egress, and recovery probe; driver or host change is never inherited evidence.' Vast is a spot marketplace. 8xH200 availability at your price point is not guaranteed hour to hour. Your single restart allowance requires a machine with matching GPU model and count to be available at a rate under the recomputed ceiling at the moment you need it. If it isn't, the route is UNFUNDED regardless of how much credit remains.
findings.evidence: 'one 8xH200 Vast host' plus 'Any offered/current rate above the recomputed ceiling refuses restart' and the G-3 requirement to rehost before disclosure.
findings.recommendation: Check 8xH200 availability and price variance on Vast over a few days before ratifying. If the market is thin, the restart allowance is theoretical. Consider whether a slightly different GPU config would be acceptable and pre-authorize it, rather than discovering the constraint when you need the replacement.

findings.title: The document's own length is an operational risk
findings.detail: This is a genuinely rigorous specification and much of the paranoia is earned — the custody analysis, the observer/wrapper MAC design, the intention-to-treat accounting, and the refusal to let abstention pass V-5 are all better than what most production systems get. But it is also long enough that no one will hold the whole thing in their head during the five-hour run, and the operational checklist (section 8) is a table of gates rather than a runbook of steps. At hour four, tired, with money burning, the person operating this needs a one-page card, not a table with a dependency DAG in a code fence.
findings.evidence: 'The operational checklist is section 8' — section 8 is a gate table with dispositions, not an ordered procedure with commands.
findings.recommendation: Write a one-page operator card before the run: the ordered commands, the three things that mean 'stop now,' the destroy command, and the phone number of the person who owns the credit card. Test that you can execute the destroy path from that card alone.

persona_reports.summary:
Look — this is one of the more carefully reasoned specifications I've seen, and I want to be clear that the paranoia is mostly earned: the custody-memory design, the refusal to let a scrubbed candidate be graded, and the honest labeling of `budget_policy_value` as a policy function with no owner are all things most teams get wrong. But the rigor is unevenly distributed. You have specified a $2.00 uncertainty floor to the cent while the actual project-killing number — the V-10 measurement census that the document itself says will "potentially substantially" exceed 660 coding cells — is deferred to a future gate with no estimate at all. The $400 is not the financial risk; it's the entry fee.

The thing I'd most want you to sit with: seventeen enumerated failure modes, every one of which terminates the route, and the single restart allowance is spent before the run begins. Your only calibration data is seven prior failures on a smaller-scoped attempt. Five hours is an allocation, not an estimate, and the document says so honestly — which means the most probable outcome of ratifying this is a Validator-custodied checkpoint that self-destructs in 30 days. That may still be worth $400 as purchased information. Just make sure you're deciding to buy information, not believing you're buying a build.

findings.title: `budget_policy_value` is defined as ownerless, but two decisions treat it as a comparable quantity against a provider-owned ceiling
findings.detail: The amendment correctly says `budget_policy_value = max(validator_derived_provider_spend, validator_elapsed_estimate)` "is not another fact and has no owner. It is a policy function evaluated fresh at each admission." Good. But then two admission tests are written as `budget_policy_value + ... <= C` and `budget_policy_value + charge_reserve + operational_contingency` reaching `C`, where `C` is a founder-authorized *local* ceiling. That is fine as a local guard, and the text says so. The defect is the *reconciliation clause*: "Every reconciliation records the provider inputs, both derivations, timestamps, rate samples, and signed delta `validator_derived_provider_spend - validator_elapsed_estimate`." Both terms of that delta are Validator-owned derivations from the *same* provider observation stream. This is not a reconciliation across an ownership boundary; it is a Validator reconciling with itself, and its threshold (`max(USD 2.00, two minutes at greatest observed rate)`) then *closes admission*. The real cross-boundary delta — Vast's settled charge versus any local estimate — is explicitly never reconciled (correctly), so the design has an enforcement mechanism pointed at an internal delta and no mechanism pointed at the boundary delta. The consequence is a false-`UNFUNDED` risk driven entirely by local estimator disagreement, not by any actual funding fact.
findings.evidence: "`budget_policy_value = max(...)` is not another fact and has no owner" / "A positive delta beyond `max(USD 2.00, two minutes at the greatest observed running rate)` closes new-turn admission." / "Vast alone owns settled provider charges"
findings.recommendation: Rename the internal delta to what it is (`estimator_divergence`) and state explicitly that it is a *self-consistency* signal about the Validator's own two derivations, not evidence about provider spend. Keep it as a diagnostic that raises `authorization_uncertainty` (which it already does) but remove its independent power to close admission — the monotone local estimate plus the uncertainty band is already the fail-closed control. As written, one estimator drifting can end a funded route while the other estimator says money remains, and the false-`UNFUNDED` apology path exists but is triggered by a defect the design created for itself.

findings.title: Notice-scope superset has no apology path for over-notification, only for under-notification
findings.detail: The design is unusually honest that after HMAC-key destruction, `UNRESOLVED_CUSTODY` means notice may be over-broad: "notification may be over-broad because absence or presence can no longer be confirmed." It then defines the possible-notice-scope superset and freezes its maximum at key destruction. There is a well-specified apology for a *missed or materially wrong* notice: "A missed or materially wrong notice receives a separately owned incident/apology record naming cause, affected parties, repair, and closing authority." But over-notification is itself a harm to a rightsholder — being told your bytes may have been disclosed when they were not is a reputational and operational cost to them, and the design deliberately guarantees it will happen sometimes. There is no owned apology, no correction record addressed to the over-noticed party, and no obligation to tell an over-noticed rightsholder later that the superset was maximal by construction rather than evidence about their bytes.
findings.evidence: "a provider-originated disclosure arriving after the required HMAC-key destruction is `UNRESOLVED_CUSTODY` by construction: notification may be over-broad because absence or presence can no longer be confirmed" — and no corresponding apology record for the over-noticed party.
findings.recommendation: Require that every `UNRESOLVED_CUSTODY` notice text itself state, to the recipient, that inclusion is by maximal-superset construction and not evidence about their specific bytes, and that this disclosure limitation was accepted in their G-8 rights grant. Add a Validator-owned `overbroad_notice_acknowledgment` record naming each recipient in the superset who was not in the observer-owned actually-sent set. That converts a knowingly-wrong guess into an apology with a named owner rather than an unowned cost pushed onto third parties.

findings.title: Two authorities claim the request-set fact: policy inventory and observer, with no stated resolution when they disagree in the deficit direction
findings.detail: The design names the split clearly: "Policy owns its authorized byte-class inventory; the independent request observer owns the exact actually-sent request-digest/count/byte-count list." And it correctly says of proxy/SSH counters, "a row they have in excess raises suspected custody for incident review, while a deficit cannot delete an observer row." That is the right asymmetry for cross-checks. But `authorized_minus_observed` — the policy-side surplus — is dispositioned only as "never proves absence and remains in the potentially-sent notice superset whenever observer/cross-check reconciliation is incomplete." There is no owner assigned to *closing* an `authorized_minus_observed` row. Every other uncertainty in this document names a resolution owner and a window (the Validator with two minutes, escalating to founder). This one silently accumulates into the notice superset forever with no one tasked to resolve it, which means the superset can only grow and the maximum-notice cardinality frozen at key destruction is inflated by unresolved bookkeeping rather than by actual custody risk.
findings.evidence: "A nonempty `authorized_minus_observed` never proves absence and remains in the potentially-sent notice superset whenever observer/cross-check reconciliation is incomplete." — no resolution owner, no window, no closure record analogous to the `Validator closure record` defined for the observed side.
findings.recommendation: Assign the Validator as resolution owner for each `authorized_minus_observed` row with the same recorded-window discipline used for `unattributed_account_delta`: classify it as (a) authorization emitted but request never constructed — closable with a local construction-side receipt before key destruction, or (b) indeterminate — stays in the superset. Without a closure path, the design's own confirmation-horizon freeze bakes in avoidable over-notification, which is the harm identified in finding 2.

findings.title: The nine-member bundle is asserted authoritative, but two members enter as digest-bound supplements admitted by the same ratification act that they help define
findings.detail: The bundle-member table lists `spec/glossary.md` and `spec/leak-runbook.md` as "digest-bound supplement," admitted by ratification of this amendment: "Ratification of this amendment admits their exact current bytes as subordinate supplemental authority." Meanwhile the reader summary says "Terms used here inherit `glossary.md`" and the precedence list places the glossary below the CLI but above the run manifest. So the glossary is load-bearing for interpreting the very amendment whose ratification grants the glossary its authority. The design partially recognizes this — the semantic-delta receipt must "enumerate every glossary term used as a load-bearing predicate" and disposition narrowing/widening under precedence — which is the right mitigation. But the circularity is not named as a residual anywhere, and the amendment defines four terms inline (`lane`, `run generation`, `admitted`, `positive control`) without stating whether those inline definitions override, agree with, or are absent from the supplement. If the glossary defines `admitted` differently, precedence says the amendment's own controls sit *below* the effective CLI but the inline definition is amendment text — an unresolved authority question at exactly the predicate that gates every gate.
findings.evidence: "in this amendment, a **lane** is one role's isolated filesystem/process authority, a **run generation** is one immutable authority and configuration binding, **admitted** means accepted by the named gate rather than merely created" versus "Terms used here inherit [`glossary.md`](glossary.md)" and glossary admitted only by this amendment's ratification.
findings.recommendation: State explicitly whether the four inline definitions supersede, restate, or are additive to the supplemental glossary, and require the G-1 semantic-delta receipt to quote the glossary's definitions of those exact four terms and record agreement or conflict. Add the bootstrap circularity as a named residual: the glossary is interpretive input to the amendment that admits it, and the founder's ratification is therefore the single act that resolves it.

findings.title: Prefix cache is authorized provider-side derived state with no owner named for its lifecycle
findings.detail: The amendment authorizes provider-side prefix caching after ratification and correctly refuses to call it erasable or recoverable: "Repo-derived prefix state is provider-accessible custody, not an erasure, privacy, durability, or recovery claim." It records the exposure class and request-digest list in the custody memory. But prefix state is *derived data outside* Guildhall, and no one is named as its owner. vLLM's persistent request/prefix caches are disabled, so this is in-process state whose lifetime is bounded by process lifetime — but the document never says that, and never says who is responsible for asserting the process boundary. When the instance is destroyed, the design says "Vast's deletion assertion is operational evidence, not proof that a provider never retained bytes" — correct for disk. For prefix state there is no equivalent statement at all. The result is a class of repo-derived data outside the trust boundary with a recorded exposure but no named authority over its existence, and therefore no apology path if a provider later reveals it persisted prefix state across instances.
findings.evidence: "prefix caching is permitted inside the explicitly authorized Vast processor boundary after ratification" and "Request and access logging, swap, CPU offload, and persistent prefix/request caches are disabled" — but no statement of who owns the prefix-state lifecycle claim or what happens if the disabled-persistence setting is wrong.
findings.recommendation: Name the Validator as owner of the *configuration assertion* (persistent prefix cache disabled, argv/env digest recorded) and state plainly that the *state itself* has no Guildhall owner and is provider-owned derived data. Add prefix state to the `provider_custody_memory` exposure classes as its own row with the explicit residual that a provider-side cross-instance persistence would be an `UNRESOLVED_CUSTODY` event under the same over-broad notice rule, since no local observer can see it. Right now the byte-level sends have an observer and the derived state does not.

findings.title: The 30-day prior-art clock has an owner and an expiry but no apology for premature destruction
findings.detail: Unadmitted prior art is retained in a "Validator-custodied, mode-0700 content-addressed manifest," clock starting at the Validator's disposition record, notice at day 21, expiry at day 30, "expiry destroys the private refs/worktree and records the manifest digest." The ownership chain is clean and the notice is a real business mechanism. The gap: if the Validator's disposition record is later found to have been recorded early — for instance because a `budget_policy_value` overestimate triggered a false `UNFUNDED` (a case the document itself anticipates and assigns a Validator-owned apology for) — the 30-day clock started on a wrong fact and the work product is already destroyed. The false-`UNFUNDED` apology exists for the money; there is none for the destroyed prior art whose retention window was computed from that same wrong disposition.
findings.evidence: "Its 30-day clock starts at the Validator's `UNFUNDED`/incomplete disposition record, not checkpoint creation." combined with "If an overestimate ended a funded route early, the Validator—not the provider—owns the false-`UNFUNDED` apology".
findings.recommendation: Make the false-`UNFUNDED` apology record explicitly enumerate any prior-art manifest whose retention clock it started, and require that a corrected disposition within the 30-day window restarts the clock from the corrected record. This costs nothing and closes the one place where an acknowledged wrong guess destroys an artifact with no owned repair.

persona_reports.summary:
The ownership discipline here is genuinely unusual — the separation of `provider_balance_observations` (Vast-owned) from the two Validator derivations, the refusal to give `budget_policy_value` an owner, the observer-owns-actually-sent versus policy-owns-authorized split, and the flat statement that destroy does not prove erasure are all exactly right, and the "cleanup code is not a business mechanism" trap is avoided almost everywhere by naming an owner and an apology record. My findings cluster on the edges of that discipline: an internal estimator disagreement that was given real enforcement power it should not have, an `authorized_minus_observed` row with no closure owner, and derived state (prefix cache) plus knowingly-over-broad notice that are recorded honestly but have no named owner or apology path.

The one I would fix first is finding 1 — the reconciliation threshold pointed at two of the Validator's own derivations can close a funded route on a fact nobody outside the Validator owns, and that is precisely the demand-for-perfect-agreement defect, just turned inward.
